title: Space-bounded quantum state testing via space-efficient quantum singular value transformation
abstractText: Abstract Driven by exploring the power of quantum computation with a limited number of qubits, we present a novel complete characterization for space-bounded quantum computation, which encompasses settings with one-sided error (unitary ) and two-sided error ( ), approached from a quantum (mixed) state testing perspective: The first family of natural complete problems for unitary $$\text {\textsf {coRQL}} $$ coRQL , namely space-bounded quantum state certification for trace distance and Hilbert–Schmidt distance; A new family of (arguably simpler) natural complete problems for , namely space-bounded quantum state testing for trace distance, Hilbert–Schmidt distance, and (von Neumann) entropy difference. In the space-bounded quantum state testing problem, we consider two logarithmic-qubit quantum circuits (devices) denoted as $$Q_0$$ Q 0 and $$Q_1$$ Q 1 , which prepare quantum states $$\rho _0$$ ρ 0 and $$\rho _1$$ ρ 1 , respectively, with access to their “source code”. Our goal is to decide whether $$\rho _0$$ ρ 0 is $$\epsilon _1$$ ϵ 1 -close to or $$\epsilon _2$$ ϵ 2 -far from $$\rho _1$$ ρ 1 with respect to a specified distance-like measure. Interestingly, unlike time-bounded state testing problems, which exhibit computational hardness depending on the chosen distance-like measure (either -complete or -complete), our results reveal that the space-bounded state testing problems, considering all three measures, are computationally as easy as preparing quantum states. Our results primarily build upon a space-efficient variant of the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) introduced by Gilyén, Su, Low, and Wiebe (STOC 2019), which is of independent interest. Our technique provides a unified approach for designing space-bounded quantum algorithms. Specifically, we show that implementing QSVT for any bounded polynomial that approximates a piecewise-smooth function incurs only a constant overhead in terms of the space required for (special forms of) the projected unitary encoding.

title: Real-Space Visualization of Site-Selective Co 3 d States in the Ising Magnet Ca 3 Co 2 O 6
abstractText: High-spin Co 3+ ions can retain a finite orbital contribution and exhibit pronounced magnetic anisotropy, providing model systems for Ising magnetism. However, direct real-space observations of their orbital states remain limited. Here, we visualize the site-dependent Co 3d electronic states in the Ising-chain magnet Ca 3 Co 2 O 6 , which contains crystallographically inequivalent high-spin and low-spin Co 3+ sites, using synchrotron X-ray diffraction and valence electron density (VED) analysis based on core differential Fourier synthesis. The octahedral Co site exhibits a VED distribution consistent with a low-spin state, whereas the trigonal-prismatic Co site shows pronounced anisotropy that cannot be reproduced by crystal electric field (CEF) effects alone. A wavefunction analysis incorporating CEF effects, spin–orbit coupling, and ligand-mediated Co 3d–O 2p–Co 4p hybridization reproduces the observed VED anisotropy. These results establish a site-selective real-space picture of the Co electronic states and demonstrate the capability of VED analysis to probe local orbital states and orbital hybridization in quantum materials.

title: EXPLORING PATH OF BUILDING "DUAL-QUALIFIED TEACHER" TEAM IN LOCAL APPLIED UNIVERSITIES
abstractText: This study explores the challenges and optimization paths in building “dual-qualified teacher” team in local applied universities, with a focus on the deep integration of theoretical and practical capabilities. By systematically analyzing the current situation, it has been found that the core obstacles are the imbalance in faculty structure, capability gaps, and insufficient institutional support. From the perspective of university-enterprise collaboration and policy linkage, this study proposes a quad-driven training framework, emphasizing the necessity of a diversified evaluation mechanism, in-depth integration of industry and education, and a tiered training system. The research shows that through structured team building, university-enterprise cooperation platforms, and innovations in incentive mechanisms, the effectiveness of “dual-qualified teacher” team can be enhanced, meeting the regional economy’s demand for application-oriented talents.

title: A Systemic Observational Framework Integrating Physiotherapy-Derived Functional, Physiological, And Behavioral Indicators In Predicting Pharmacological Response
abstractText: Background: Inter-individual variability in pharmacological response remains a persistent challenge in clinical rehabilitation. While pharmacokinetic and molecular mechanisms are well established, they account for only a proportion of observed outcome variability. Functional performance, physiological regulation, and behavioral engagement—core domains of physiotherapy—are increasingly recognized as influential determinants of therapeutic response. Aim: To develop and describe a systemic observational framework integrating physiotherapy-derived functional, physiological, and behavioral indicators with pharmacological response, supported by descriptive statistical reasoning. Methodology: A conceptual observational methodology was adopted. Peer-reviewed literature was synthesized, and commonly reported trends, proportions, and associations were interpreted using descriptive and inferential statistical logic (e.g., variability, correlation strength, explained variance), without primary data collection. Results: Evidence across rehabilitation and pharmacological literature consistently indicates that functional and behavioral variables account for a substantial proportion of outcome variability unexplained by pharmacological parameters alone. Descriptive trends suggest moderate-to-strong associations between autonomic regulation, movement efficiency, behavioral engagement, and therapeutic stability. Conclusion: Incorporating physiotherapy-derived indicators into pharmacological interpretation enhances explanatory power and clinical relevance. A systemic, statistically informed observational framework supports personalized, interdisciplinary healthcare.

title: The Role of Self-Awareness, Self-Control, and Spirituality in the Prevention of Social Harms Among Youth
abstractText: Objective: This study aimed to examine the role of self-awareness, self-control, and spirituality in the prevention of social harms among youth. Methods and Materials: A descriptive-correlational design with a predictive modeling approach was used. The sample consisted of 350 young people aged 18 to 29 years selected through multistage cluster sampling. Data were collected using the Self-Reflection and Insight Scale, Brief Self-Control Scale, Spiritual Well-Being Scale, Iranian Adolescents Risk-Taking Scale, and a demographic information form. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficients, hierarchical multiple regression, and structural equation modeling. Findings: Self-awareness, self-control, and spirituality were negatively associated with vulnerability to social harms (r = -.43, -.58, and -.49, respectively; p < .001). The hierarchical regression model was significant, F(6, 343) = 42.78, p < .001, and explained 42.8% of the variance. Self-control was the strongest negative predictor (β = -.37, p < .001), followed by spirituality (β = -.26, p < .001) and self-awareness (β = -.18, p = .002). The structural model showed acceptable fit, χ²/df = 2.22, CFI = .94, TLI = .92, RMSEA = .059, and SRMR = .046. Conclusion: Self-awareness, self-control, and spirituality appear to be important protective factors against vulnerability to social harms among youth. Prevention programs should strengthen reflective capacity, impulse regulation, meaning-making, and value-based decision-making.

title: The Effectiveness of Group-Based Positive Youth Development Training on Attachment to Parents and Alexithymia in Male Adolescents with a Tendency Toward Addiction in Isfahan
abstractText: Objective: This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of group-based Positive Youth Development training on attachment to parents and alexithymia among male adolescents with a tendency toward addiction in Isfahan. Methods and Materials: This quasi-experimental study used a pretest–posttest–follow-up design with a control group. The statistical population included male lower-secondary students with a tendency toward addiction in Isfahan during the 2023–2024 academic year. Thirty eligible adolescents were selected through purposive sampling and randomly assigned to experimental and control groups. The experimental group received twelve 90-minute weekly sessions of Positive Youth Development training, while the control group remained on a waiting list. Data were collected using the Inventory of Parent and Peer Attachment and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance and Bonferroni post-hoc tests. Findings: Repeated-measures ANOVA indicated a significant time effect for attachment to mother, attachment to father, and alexithymia. The results showed that the intervention produced a significant improvement in attachment to mother and a significant reduction in alexithymia from pretest to posttest and follow-up. However, the between-group effect for attachment to father was not significant, and Bonferroni comparisons confirmed that changes in attachment to father were not statistically meaningful. The intervention effects for attachment to mother and alexithymia remained stable at follow-up. Conclusion: Group-based Positive Youth Development training can be considered an effective preventive and corrective intervention for improving attachment to mothers and reducing alexithymia in male adolescents with a tendency toward addiction. However, improving attachment to fathers may require longer, family-based, or father-inclusive interventions.

title: Designing a Curriculum Model Based on Artificial Intelligence and Purposeful Physical Activity to Enhance Learning Self-Regulation, Mental Health, and Psychological Well-Being among Students
abstractText: Objective: The objective of this study was to design and validate a curriculum model based on artificial intelligence and purposeful physical activity with emphasis on enhancing learning self-regulation, mental health, and psychological well-being among students. Methods and Materials: This applied developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, 20 experts in curriculum studies, educational technology, artificial intelligence in education, physical education, educational psychology, and student mental health were selected through purposive criterion-based sampling from Tehran and participated in semi-structured interviews. The interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis to extract the main dimensions, components, and indicators of the proposed curriculum model. In the quantitative phase, 384 secondary school students from Tehran were selected through multistage cluster sampling during the 2025–2026 academic year. Data were collected using a researcher-made curriculum model validation questionnaire, a learning self-regulation questionnaire, the General Health Questionnaire, and a psychological well-being scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. Findings: The inferential findings showed that the final curriculum model had acceptable empirical fit. The final modified model demonstrated favorable fit indices, including χ²/df = 2.14, GFI = 0.917, AGFI = 0.901, CFI = 0.951, TLI = 0.944, RMSEA = 0.054, and SRMR = 0.043. Artificial intelligence-based curriculum components had significant direct effects on learning self-regulation, mental health, and psychological well-being. Purposeful physical activity also had significant direct effects on learning self-regulation, mental health, and psychological well-being. Learning self-regulation and mental health significantly predicted psychological well-being. The model explained 48% of the variance in learning self-regulation, 43% of the variance in mental health, and 57% of the variance in psychological well-being. Conclusion: The findings indicate that an integrated curriculum model based on artificial intelligence and purposeful physical activity can provide an effective educational framework for strengthening students’ self-regulated learning, supporting mental health, and promoting psychological well-being.

title: The Effectiveness of Emotion-Focused Therapy in Improving Psychological Flexibility and Zest for Life Among University Students Who Have Experienced a Romantic Breakup
abstractText: Objective: This study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of emotion-focused therapy in improving psychological flexibility and zest for life among university students who had experienced a romantic breakup. Methods and Materials: This study employed a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design with a follow-up assessment. The statistical population comprised all university students in Birjand who had experienced a romantic breakup during the 2025–2026 academic year. Participants were recruited through convenience sampling, and 30 eligible students were selected based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria and randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 15) or a control group (n = 15). The research instruments included the Psychological Flexibility Questionnaire (2010) and the Zest for Life After Romantic Breakup Questionnaire (Shomali & Barkhordari, 2026). The experimental group received group-based emotion-focused therapy in eight 90-minute sessions held twice weekly, whereas the control group received no intervention during this period. The data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance and the Bonferroni post hoc test. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS version 27. Findings: The results indicated that emotion-focused therapy had a significant effect on increasing psychological flexibility and zest for life among university students who had experienced a romantic breakup (p < .01). These effects were also maintained at the one-month follow-up assessment, and the differences between the experimental and control groups remained statistically significant for both variables (p < .05). Conclusion: Based on the findings, emotion-focused therapy can be used as an effective intervention to improve psychological flexibility and enhance zest for life among university students who have experienced a romantic breakup. It is recommended that this therapeutic approach be implemented systematically within university psychological and counseling services, particularly for students experiencing emotional distress following romantic breakups.

title: The Mediating Role of Self-Injurious Thoughts in the Relationship Between Psychological Distress and Death Obsession with Suicide Attempts Among Adolescents Experiencing War Anxiety
abstractText: Objective: This study aimed to examine the mediating role of self-injurious thoughts in the relationship between psychological distress and death obsession with suicide attempts among adolescents experiencing war anxiety. Methods and Materials: This applied study was conducted using a correlational design based on structural equation modeling. The statistical sample consisted of 215 adolescents aged 15 to 18 years living in Mahshahr, who were selected through voluntary sampling. The research instruments included the Shomali and Barkhordari War Anxiety Questionnaire, the Osman et al. Suicide Attempt Questionnaire, the Abdel-Khalek Death Obsession Scale, the Kessler et al. Psychological Distress Scale, and the Shomali and Barkhordari Self-Injurious Thoughts Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation and structural equation modeling through SPSS version 27 and AMOS version 24. Findings: The inferential results showed that the direct effects of psychological distress and self-injurious thoughts on suicide attempts were positive and statistically significant. The direct effects of psychological distress and death obsession on self-injurious thoughts were also positive and statistically significant. In addition, the indirect effects of psychological distress and death obsession on suicide attempts through self-injurious thoughts were positive and statistically significant. However, the direct effect of death obsession on suicide attempts was not significant in the final structural model. These findings confirmed the mediating role of self-injurious thoughts in the relationship between psychological distress, death obsession, and suicide attempts among adolescents experiencing war anxiety. Conclusion: The findings indicate that self-injurious thoughts are a key cognitive-emotional mechanism linking psychological distress and death obsession to suicide attempts in adolescents exposed to war-related anxiety. Therefore, preventive and therapeutic interventions should prioritize the early identification and modification of self-injurious thoughts, especially among vulnerable adolescents experiencing psychological distress and death-related preoccupations.

title: The Relationship of Classroom Emotion, Self-Compassion, and Tolerance of Ambiguity with Academic Anxiety among Female Senior High School Students in District 9 of Karaj
abstractText: Objective: This study aimed to examine the relationship of classroom emotion, self-compassion, and tolerance of ambiguity with academic anxiety among female senior high school students in District 9 of Karaj. Methods and Materials: The present study employed a descriptive-correlational research design. The statistical population consisted of female senior high school students in District 9 of Karaj, from whom 210 students were selected initially through multistage cluster sampling and finally through convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Friedman and Jacob Test Anxiety Questionnaire (1997), the Classroom Emotion Questionnaire developed by Titsworth et al. (2010), the Tolerance of Ambiguity Questionnaire developed by Weden et al. (2003), and the Short Form of the Self-Compassion Scale developed by Raes et al. (2011). The collected data were analyzed using descriptive indices, Pearson correlation coefficient, and stepwise multiple regression analysis. Findings: The inferential findings indicated a significant negative relationship between classroom emotion and academic anxiety, suggesting that more positive classroom emotional experiences were associated with lower levels of academic anxiety. A significant negative relationship was also found between self-compassion and academic anxiety, indicating that students with higher self-compassion experienced lower academic anxiety. In the stepwise regression analysis, classroom emotion emerged as the strongest predictor and explained 15.50% of the variance in academic anxiety. Self-compassion was added in the second step and explained an additional 2.20% of the variance. Together, classroom emotion and self-compassion accounted for 17.70% of the total variance in academic anxiety. Tolerance of ambiguity did not enter the final predictive model. Conclusion: The findings suggest that classroom emotion and self-compassion are important psychological and educational variables in predicting academic anxiety among female senior high school students. Strengthening positive classroom emotional experiences and promoting self-compassion may help reduce students’ academic anxiety.

title: The Mediating Role of Moral Development and Religious Orientation in the Relationship of Narcissism and Bullying with Academic Cheating among Upper Secondary School Students
abstractText: Objective: This study aimed to model the effects of narcissism and bullying on academic cheating through the mediating roles of moral development and religious orientation among upper secondary school students. Methods and Materials: This applied correlational study was conducted among upper secondary school students in Zanjan during the 2024–2025 academic year. A total of 311 students, including 167 boys and 144 girls, were selected using multistage cluster sampling. Data were collected using Murdock and Stephens’ Academic Cheating Questionnaire, the 16-item Narcissistic Personality Inventory by Ames, Rose, and Anderson, the Illinois Bullying Scale by Espelage and Holt, Manavipour’s Moral Development Scale, and Allport and Ross’s Religious Orientation Scale. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficients, path analysis, and bootstrap testing in SPSS version 28 and AMOS version 24. Findings: The proposed model demonstrated acceptable fit indices (GFI = 0.90, CFI = 0.90, RMSEA = 0.053). Narcissism positively and significantly predicted academic cheating (β = 0.168, p = 0.003), and bullying also positively and significantly predicted academic cheating (β = 0.274, p < 0.001). Moral development negatively predicted academic cheating (β = -0.202, p < 0.001). Intrinsic religious orientation (β = -0.181, p < 0.001) and extrinsic religious orientation (β = -0.187, p < 0.001) also negatively and significantly predicted academic cheating. Narcissism (β = -0.270, p < 0.001) and bullying (β = -0.320, p < 0.001) negatively predicted moral development. Indirect effect analysis showed that moral development significantly mediated the relationships between narcissism (β = 0.054, p = 0.002) and bullying (β = 0.065, p < 0.001) with academic cheating. Intrinsic and extrinsic religious orientation also showed significant mediating effects. Conclusion: The findings indicate that moral development and religious orientation function as protective mechanisms in the relationships of narcissism and bullying with academic cheating. Preventive and educational interventions aimed at reducing academic cheating may benefit from strengthening moral reasoning, empathy, moral self-regulation, and the internalization of religious values among upper secondary school students.

title: Prediction of Cognitive Flexibility Based on Attention Control, Working Memory, and Problem-Solving Skills in Adolescents Using CatBoost
abstractText: Objective: The present study aimed to predict cognitive flexibility based on attention control, working memory, and problem-solving skills in adolescents using the CatBoost machine learning algorithm. Methods and Materials: This study was conducted using a quantitative, descriptive-correlational, and predictive design. The statistical population included adolescents studying in secondary schools in Tehran during the 2025–2026 academic year. The final sample consisted of 384 adolescents selected through multistage cluster sampling. Data were collected using standardized self-report instruments measuring cognitive flexibility, attention control, working memory, and problem-solving skills. After preliminary data screening, descriptive indices, reliability coefficients, Pearson correlation coefficients, and machine learning-based predictive analyses were conducted. The CatBoost algorithm was used to predict cognitive flexibility, and the dataset was divided into training and test subsets. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, mean squared error, root mean squared error, coefficient of determination, and five-fold cross-validation. Feature importance analysis was also performed to determine the relative contribution of each predictor. Findings: The results showed that cognitive flexibility had significant positive correlations with problem-solving skills (r = 0.61, p < 0.01), attention control (r = 0.55, p < 0.01), and working memory (r = 0.48, p < 0.01). The CatBoost model demonstrated acceptable predictive accuracy. In the training set, the model explained 76.5% of the variance in cognitive flexibility, while in the test set, it explained 65.2% of the variance. The cross-validation results also supported the stability of the model, with an average R² of 0.636. Feature importance analysis indicated that problem-solving skills had the highest predictive contribution, followed by attention control and working memory. Conclusion: The findings indicate that cognitive flexibility in adolescents can be meaningfully predicted by problem-solving skills, attention control, and working memory. The CatBoost algorithm provided an effective predictive model and showed that problem-solving skills were the most important predictor.

title: INOVASI PENGOLAHAN BUAH NAGA MENJADI SELAI GUNA MENINGKATKAN NILAI EKONOMI MASYARAKAT DESA PERBAJI
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji inovasi pengolahan buah naga menjadi selai sebagai upaya memanfaatkan komoditas lokal dan meningkatkan nilai ekonomi masyarakat Desa Perbaji. Permasalahan penelitian berangkat dari pemanfaatan buah naga yang masih dominan dalam bentuk segar, sedangkan buah hortikultura memiliki daya simpan yang terbatas sehingga diperlukan diversifikasi produk. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Participatory Action Research (PAR) dengan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif. Masyarakat dilibatkan secara langsung dalam proses pengenalan potensi, perencanaan, praktik pengolahan, pengemasan, dan evaluasi kegiatan. Data diperoleh melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa buah naga dapat diolah menjadi selai melalui beberapa tahapan sederhana, yaitu persiapan bahan, penghancuran, pemasakan, pendinginan, dan pengemasan. Kegiatan ini memberikan pengalaman praktis kepada masyarakat dalam mengolah buah naga menjadi produk turunan yang memiliki peluang untuk dikembangkan sebagai pangan lokal. Pengembangan produk masih memerlukan perbaikan pada konsistensi produk, kemasan, daya simpan, penetapan harga, dan strategi pemasaran. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa inovasi pengolahan buah naga dapat menjadi salah satu bentuk pemberdayaan masyarakat berbasis potensi lokal sekaligus membuka peluang peningkatan nilai ekonomi.

title: MANAJEMEN PROGRAM DAKWAH DALAM MENINGKATKAN AKHLAKUL KARIMAH SANTRI DI PANTI ASUHAN AL-WASLIYAH
abstractText: Panti asuhan tidak hanya memiliki tanggung jawab dalam memenuhi kebutuhan fisik anak, tetapi juga berperan dalam membangun perkembangan spiritual, moral, dan sosial. Dalam praktiknya, pengelolaan panti sering lebih berorientasi pada pemenuhan kebutuhan dasar, sedangkan pembinaan akhlak belum selalu dilaksanakan melalui program yang terstruktur dan berkelanjutan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis manajemen program dakwah dalam pembinaan akhlakul karimah santri di Panti Asuhan Al-Wasliyah Jalan Ismailiyah serta merumuskan bentuk pengelolaan program yang lebih terarah. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis penelitian lapangan dan sifat deskriptif analitik. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi partisipatif non-aktif, dan dokumentasi terhadap pengurus, pengasuh, serta perwakilan santri. Analisis data menggunakan model interaktif Miles, Huberman, dan Saldana melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan, dengan triangulasi teknik dan sumber untuk menjaga keabsahan data. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa fungsi perencanaan, pengorganisasian, pelaksanaan, dan pengawasan diterapkan dalam pengelolaan program dakwah. Program pembinaan meliputi shalat berjamaah, kajian akhlak, tahfiz dan tahsin Al-Qur’an, kultum, pembinaan adab harian, serta gotong royong. Penelitian juga menunjukkan pentingnya manajemen waktu dan penyusunan anggaran yang sistematis bagi keberlanjutan program dakwah dan pembentukan akhlak santri.

title: CIRCUIT TRAINING IMPLEMENTATION IN INDONESIAN ARMY PHYSICAL EDUCATION A QUALITATIVE CASE STUDY
abstractText: Abstrak Penelitian ini mengkaji pelaksanaan pembinaan kesegaran jasmani dan latihan sirkuit di Dinas Jasmani Angkatan Darat, Cimahi, Jawa Barat. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan desain studi kasus dan melibatkan 44 informan yang dipilih secara purposif, terdiri atas satu pimpinan institusi, lima kepala seksi, 35 prajurit, dan tiga pakar atau atlet olahraga. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara terstruktur, dan analisis dokumen, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Triangulasi digunakan untuk memeriksa kredibilitas temuan. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa program telah memiliki jadwal dan standar penilaian, tetapi pelaksanaannya menghadapi rutinitas latihan berulang, keterbatasan penyesuaian beban individu, dan gangguan partisipasi akibat tuntutan tugas. Informan mengaitkan latihan sirkuit dengan variasi aktivitas dan keterlibatan kelompok. Temuan tersebut merupakan persepsi informan, bukan bukti peningkatan fisiologis. Kontribusi penelitian terletak pada penjelasan kontekstual mengenai kesenjangan antara pengaturan program dan pelaksanaan latihan yang adaptif. Pengembangan modul, pemantauan beban, dan penguatan kompetensi pelatih direkomendasikan untuk diuji lebih lanjut. Kata kunci: Latihan Sirkuit; Pendidikan Jasmani Militer; Implementasi Pelatihan; Individualisasi Beban Latihan; TNI Angkatan Darat Abstract Keywords: Qur’an memorization; boarding program; full-day program; tahfidz implementation; learning supervision; school–family partnership.This study examines physical fitness development and circuit training implementation at the Army Physical Training Service in Cimahi, West Java. A descriptive qualitative case study involved 44 purposively selected informants: one institutional leader, five section heads, 35 soldiers, and three sports experts or athletes. Data were collected through observation, structured interviews, and document analysis and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Triangulation supported credibility. The findings identify an established system of training schedules and assessment standards alongside repetitive routines, limited workload individualization, and participation disrupted by operational duties. Informants associated circuit training with exercise variety and group engagement; these accounts indicate perceived benefits rather than measured physiological improvement. Instructor competence, equipment availability, and supervision were identified as relevant implementation conditions. The study offers a contextual account of the gap between formal program organization and adaptive delivery in military physical education. Adaptable training modules, workload monitoring, and instructor development are proposed for subsequent evaluation. The single institutional case does not establish effectiveness or prevalence across the Indonesian Army. title: Gross Morphometry and Histometry of Pancreas in Postnatal Indian Pigs (Sus scrofa domesticus)
abstractText: The present study was conducted to evaluate the gross morphometry and histometry of the pancreas in different postnatal age groups of Indian domestic pigs (Sus scrofa domesticus) such as pancreas weight, pancreatic lobes length and width, capsule thickness, acini and islet diameter. Pancreases were collected from 18 apparently healthy animals irrespective of sex from local slaughter houses in and around Hyderabad and were categorized into three age groups: Group I (0-4 weeks), Group II (4-10 weeks), Group III (>10 weeks) with six specimens in each group. The pancreas weight showed progressive increase with advancing age with the lowest value recorded in Group I (0-4 weeks) and the highest in Group III (>10 weeks) with highly significant difference among groups. A strong positive correlation was also observed between body weight and pancreas weight (p=0.991). The mean length of pancreatic lobes increased progressively and significantly with the advancing age with greatest lobe length recorded in splenic lobe of Group III (12.08 ± 0.84 cm) and least length in connecting lobe of Group I (2.42 ± 0.46 cm). The mean width of all the pancreatic lobes increased progressively with advancing age with greatest width noticed in splenic lobe (4.62 ± 0.50 cm) of Group III and least width in duodenal lobe of Group I (0.88 ± 0.22 cm). The study provides basic information, which is very useful for identification of any pathological changes and for further studies such as porcine islet transplantation. Histometry included capsule thickness, acini and islet diameter of which capsule thickness increased significantly (p = 0.005) from 116.89 ± 13.74 µm (Group I) to 337.49 ± 41.12 µm (Group III). Acinar diameter and Islet diameter showed an increase in all the lobes from Group I to Group III. The splenic lobe showed a significant age-related differences in acinar diameter (p= 0.005) and islet diameter (p=0.008), whereas the connecting and duodenal lobes showed no significant differences. Thus, post-natally pancreas undergone gross and histological changes.

title: Estimation of Genetic Parameters of Important Economic Traits in Ankaleshwar Breed of Chicken
abstractText: The present investigation was carried out with the performance records of Ankaleshwar birds spanning one generation to estimate genetic parameters of economically important traits. A mixed linear model was employed for the analysis, incorporating sire as a random effect and mean as fixed effect. The performance traits included age at first egg (AFE), egg weight at 28 weeks of age (EW28) and 40 week of age (EW40), body weight at 16 weeks of age (BW16) and 40 weeks of age (BW40), egg number up to 40 weeks (TEN40). Highly significant (p≤0.01) effect of sire was observed on all traits, except EW28 and EW40. The least squares means for performance traits AFE, EW28, EW40, BW16, BW40 and TEN40 were 150.78±0.38 days, 38.22±0.10 g, 42.94±0.10 g, 962.21±4.07 g, 1556.20±7.01 g and 83.47±0.51 eggs, respectively. The heritability estimates were low to moderate for all the traits. The age at first egg was negatively associated with egg weight at 40 weeks (r=-0.81) and total egg production up to 40 weeks (r=-0.67). Further, body weight at 16 weeks of age had strong association with body weight of 40 weeks (r=0.93). There were positive genetic associations of egg weight at 40 weeks with body weight at 40 weeks (r=0.74) and total egg production up to 40 weeks (r=0.50). These findings emphasize that incorporating early measurable traits and key reproductive indicators along with their correlated responses is essential for developing an efficient and sustainable breeding programme to improve egg production and overall productivity in Ankaleshwar breed of chicken.

title: Carbon Dioxide Cryoepilation for Canine Distichiasis: A Report of Four Cases
abstractText: Distichiasis is a clinically significant eyelid disorder in dogs, characterized by the abnormal emergence of cilia from the meibomian gland openings rather than the normal eyelash line. These ectopic hairs though sometimes asymptomatic frequently cause ocular irritation through constant friction against the corneal surface. Clinical manifestations range from mild epiphora, conjunctivitis to severe blepharospasm and corneal ulceration which can compromise vision and quality of life (Marchini et al., 2024). The condition is reported more commonly in predisposed exotic breeds, those are suspected to have a hereditary basis although the exact mode of inheritance remains unclear (Verloop and Read, 2023). As per the authors experience, it is also seen in Rajapalayam and non-descript dogs. Conventional management strategies including manual epilation provide only temporary relief due to follicular persistence, while surgical and non-surgical permanent techniques often carry risks of scarring, eyelid distortion or pigmentary changes (Singh, 2002; Verloop and Read, 2023). Cryoepilation has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative offering targeted follicular destruction with preservation of eyelid anatomy (Verloop and Read, 2023; Reynolds et al., 2023). The present case series documents the clinical management of eight eyes (4 canine patients) with distichiasis using carbon dioxide-based cryoepilation as an effective practical option for permanent resolution of distichiasis.

title: Clinico-Therapeutic Management of Parascariasis in Foals
abstractText: The present study of clinico-therapeutics management of parascariasis in foals was carried out amongst the foals presented from different villages of Bhavnagar districts. A total of 12 foals were selected based on the clinical finding and confirmatory diagnosis of the presence of Parascaris spp. worm eggs in faecal smear by sedimentation methods. Clinical findings revealed roughened hair coat, loose consistency of faeces, undigested feed particles in faeces, weight loss, weakness and loss of skin elasticity. Haematological findings revealed significantly decreased haemoglobin, pack cell volume, total erythrocyte count and total leukocyte counts. All the 12 foals were successfully treated with Fenbendazole @ 7.5 mg/kg once in a day for five days along with supportive therapy.

title: Surgical Management of Neurofibroma with Cystic Endometrial Hyperplasia in a Labrador Female Dog
abstractText: Canine genital tumours are rare, accounting for 3.0-4.0% of all tumours, and primarily affect intact females, with most occurring in the vagina and vulva rather than the uterus (8:1 ratio) (Thacher and Bradley, 1983). Most vaginal tumours (73-94%) are benign and reported occasionally (Salomon et al., 2004; Balamurugan and Sivasudharsan, 2021). Typical clinical signs include a visible protruding mass, vulvar discharge, dysuria, and tenesmus (Withrow and Susaneck, 1986). Some vaginal tumor may be treated with aglepristone or vincristine sulphate, and surgical approaches include episiotomy and excision of the tumorous mass, or more aggressive procedures such as vaginectomy, urethroplasty, and ventral pelvic osteotomy (Salomon et al., 2004; Rollon et al., 2008; Verma et al., 2019). Ovariohysterectomy may be performed to prevent recurrence of the tumourous mass, which may be due to hormonal imbalance. The cystic endometrial hyperplasia/pyometra complex is a severe, poly-systemic diestrual disorder of intact bitches, characterized by endometrial hyperplasia and inflammatory cell infiltration (Veiga et al., 2017). The pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving abnormal uterine responses to progesterone and estrogen (De Bosschere et al., 2001), IGF-1-stimulated endometrial growth, matrix metalloproteinase-mediated remodelling and Escherichia coli colonization via specific endometrial receptors (Schlafer and Gifford, 2008). While CEH and pyometra can present as distinct disorders (Hagman et al., 2009), hyperplastic secretory activity frequently results in sterile fluid accumulation (mucometra/hydrometra) or bacterial pyometra. Affected bitches commonly present with inappetence, vomiting, polyuria/polydipsia, and abdominal distension (Smith, 2006). Ultrasonography confirms the diagnosis, and total ovariohysterectomy (OHE) is the treatment of choice; medical management with prostaglandin F2α carries a risk of uterine rupture or recurrence (Gobello et al., 2003; Gumber et al., 2010). Local surgical excision via episiotomy, coupled with ovariohysterectomy (OHE), is curative for benign genital tumours and prevents recurrence. The present document reports case of a bitch with a neurofibroma along with CEH that was successfully managed surgically.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance Profiling of Shiga Toxin-Producing Escherichia coli Isolated from Diarrhoeic Cattle
abstractText: Cattle are recognized as important reservoirs of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC), contributing to the transmission of antimicrobial-resistant strains through the food chain and environment. The present study investigated the phenotypic and genotypic antimicrobial resistance profiles of 40 molecularly confirmed STEC isolates recovered from diarrhoeic cattle in Jaipur, Rajasthan. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed against 11 antimicrobial agents using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method. The highest susceptibility was observed against ampicillin/sulbactam, doxycycline, imipenem and chloramphenicol (80% each), whereas the highest resistance was detected against ciprofloxacin (97.5%), nitrofurantoin (95%) and co-trimoxazole (90%). Multidrug resistance was observed in 39 (97.5%) isolates, and resistotyping revealed 24 distinct resistance patterns, with R-1 as the predominant profile (25.0%). Molecular analysis detected tetA and blaTEM resistance genes in 17.5% and 15.0% of isolates, respectively. The coexistence of virulence-associated STEC with multidrug resistance highlights the potential public health risk posed by cattle as reservoirs of antimicrobial-resistant zoonotic pathogens. These findings emphasize the importance of antimicrobial stewardship, continuous surveillance and One Health approaches to control the emergence and spread of resistant STEC in livestock populations.

title: Clinical Management of Endometritis in a Mare: A Case Report
abstractText: Equine endometritis is an inflammatory condition of the uterus mainly caused by contamination of the uterine lumen with microorganisms, debris, or abnormal substances, which may originate from pathogenic bacteria, reproductive tract defects (such as pneumovagina and urovagina), poor perineal conformation, or unhygienic management practices during breeding and parturition (LeBlanc, 2010; Brinsko, 2011; Christoffersen and Troedsson, 2017). It is a complex disorder involving both physiological and pathological responses; normally, mares develop a transient inflammatory reaction after breeding (acute post-breeding endometritis) that clears contaminants within 24-48 h, creating a favourable environment for embryo survival (Morris et al., 2020). However, failure of this clearance mechanism leads to persistent forms such as persistent post-mating endometritis or chronic infectious endometritis, which impair fertility and increase embryonic loss (Malschitzky et al., 2003; Brinsko, 2011). Since the embryo enters the uterus around 6-7 days post-ovulation, timely resolution of inflammation is essential, as prolonged inflammation characterized by uterine fluid accumulation and cytokine activity reduces embryo viability (Robertson et al., 2018). Diagnosis of endometritis in mares is commonly achieved through ultrasonography, uterine cytology, microbial culture and in some cases, endometrial biopsy. Therapeutic management typically involves uterine lavage, administration of appropriate antimicrobial agents, use of ecbolic drugs to enhance uterine clearance and correction of predisposing anatomical defects, such as performing Caslick’s surgery (Samper, 2009; Dascanio and McCue, 2014). Overall, effective management depends on early diagnosis, proper hygiene and targeted therapeutic strategies to improve reproductive efficiency in mares (LeBlanc, 2010; Scoggin, 2016). This document reports on the successful clinical management of endometritis in a mare.

title: Successful Diagnosis and Treatment of Naso-Sinual Myxosarcoma in a Dog
abstractText: Nasal and paranasal sinus tumours are relatively uncommon in dogs, accounting for approximately 1-2% of all canine neoplasms. However, they constitute the majority of tumours affecting the upper respiratory tract in dogs (Withrow et al., 2020). These tumours are predominantly malignant and locally invasive, leading to progressive destruction of surrounding soft tissues and bony structures of the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses (Thrall and LaRue, 1995). Clinical manifestations commonly include unilateral or bilateral nasal discharge, epistaxis, sneezing, facial deformity, stertor and dyspnoea (Ettinger et al., 2017). Carcinomas are the most commonly reported canine nasal tumours, whereas sarcomas occur less frequently (Meuten, 2017). Myxo-sarcomas are classified as soft tissue sarcomas of fibroblast origin with an abundant myxoid matrix composed of mucopolysaccharides (Meuten, 2017). The prognosis is generally poor because of the high rates of local recurrence and metastasis (Gage et al., 2019). Advanced diagnostic modalities such as rhinoscopy and computed tomography (CT) are important for evaluation of tumour extent, turbinate destruction and sinus involvement (Adams et al., 2009). Histopathological examination remains the gold standard for definitive diagnosis. Therapeutic approaches commonly involve surgery, radiation therapy and chemotherapy either alone or in combination depending upon tumour type and extent of disease (Dernell et al., 1998). The present case report describes the clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, surgical management and chemotherapeutic treatment of naso-sinusal myxosarcoma in a dog.

title: MECHANISTIC EVALUATION AND ANALYTICAL MITIGATION OF EXCIPIENT-INDUCED IN-SITU NITROSAMINE FORMATION IN SOLID ORAL DOSAGE FORMS: AN INTEGRATED FORMULATION AND VALIDATED CHROMATOGRAPHIC CONTROL STRATEGY
abstractText: Background: Recurring international recalls of essential oral solid dosage forms contaminated with Nitrosamine Drug Substance-Related Impurities (NDSRIs) expose a fundamental vulnerability in conventional tablet manufacturing. Trace inorganic nitrites (0.1–10.0 µg/g) present across widely used excipients like crospovidone and microcrystalline cellulose react directly with vulnerable secondary amine drugs during standard processing and routine shelf storage. Objective: Here, we developed an economically practical, scalable formulation strategy to suppress excipient-mediated nitrosamine formation using food-grade antioxidant scavengers, paired with an accessible isocratic reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC-UV) analytical control method validated strictly against ICH Q2(R2) and ICH Q14 requirements. Methods: Propranolol hydrochloride served as a representative aliphatic secondary amine (pKa = 9.45). Direct-compression binary powder mixtures were spiked with 5.0 µg/g sodium nitrite at microenvironmental pH 3.0, then incubated under accelerated thermal stress (60.0°C ± 1.0°C for 48 hours). We tested the protective capacity of L-ascorbic acid (0.1% and 0.5% w/w) against L-histidine (0.5% w/w). Chromatographic resolution was carried out on an Inertsil ODS-3V C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) using an isocratic mobile phase of acetonitrile and 25 mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 3.00 ± 0.05) (55:45, v/v) at 1.0 mL/min with photodiode array detection at 290 nm. Results: Positive control blends generated substantial quantities of N-nitroso-propranolol (NNP; mean peak area 142,580 ± 1,820 mAU·s). Incorporating 0.5% w/w L-ascorbic acid suppressed NNP formation by 98.70% ± 0.06% (p < 0.0001), while 0.5% w/w L-histidine yielded 92.30% ± 0.16% inhibition. Our chromatographic assay satisfied every ICH Q2(R2) requirement: linearity spanned 10.0–150.0 µg/mL (R² = 0.9996), system repeatability remained tight at 0.68% RSD, recovery ranged between 99.12% and 100.82%, with limits of detection and quantification established at 0.42 µg/mL and 1.28 µg/mL, respectively. During 6-month accelerated stability testing (40°C ± 2°C / 75% ± 5% RH), finished tablets retained NNP levels at 0.28 ppm (44.8 ng/day daily intake), leaving a 33.5-fold safety margin below the US FDA limit of 1500 ng/day. Conclusion: Blending 0.5% w/w ascorbic acid offers an accessible, zero-cost-penalty platform that halts mutagenic nitrosation well below global regulatory thresholds, without disturbing tablet hardness, disintegration, or dissolution behavior.

title: Non-Invasive Diagnosis and Retrospective Evaluation of Pulmonary Metastasis in Canines
abstractText: Pulmonary metastasis is a frequent complication of malignant tumours in dogs. Dogs (n=112) diagnosed with pulmonary metastasis in Radiography and Computed Tomography (CT) between August 2024 and July 2025 at MVC Teaching Hospital, Chennai were analysed, retrospectively. Insides of pulmonary metastasis were categorised with respect to sex, breed, age, and lesion with respect to radiographic patterns. Out of 112 cases, 43 were males (38.4%) and 69 were females (61.6%). The most affected breeds were non-descriptive (51), German Shepherd (9), Labrador (18), Spitz (8), Doberman (7), Golden Retriever (4), Shitzhu (4), Rottweiler (3), and others (9). Lesion patterns included diffuse miliary (61), local miliary (32), intra-thoracic mass (8), mediastinal mass (4), nodular lesions (5), and pulmonary osteomata (2). Age distribution showed 1-5 years (16 cases), 5-10 years (46 cases) and 10-15 years (45 cases) were the most affected, with only 5 dogs over 15 years. Fourteen canines were subjected to CT in addition to radiography to reveal the root cause of pulmonary metastasis and its sensitivity. Findings highlight a female predominance, a higher occurrence in middle-aged to geriatric dogs, and the diffuse miliary pattern as the most common radiographic manifestation.

title: Tumours of Urogenital System in Dogs
abstractText: A total of 10 canine urogenital tumour cases were evaluated for their clinical, haemato-biochemical, radiographic, ultrasonographic, cytological, and histopathological features. The cases included five canine transmissible venereal tumours (CTVT), four vaginal tumours, and one cryptorchid testicular tumour. CTVT occurred in younger dogs (3.9 ± 1.27 years) as ulcerated, cauliflower-like genital masses, whereas vaginal tumours affected older dogs (11.75 ± 1.43 years) and presented as protruding vulvar masses. The cryptorchid testicular tumour was diagnosed in a 7-year-old German Shepherd dog. Mild leukocytosis was observed initially in CTVT cases, with a significant reduction following vincristine therapy, while haemoglobin and erythrocyte values remained within normal limits. Cytology confirmed CTVT, whereas histopathology with Masson’s Trichome staining identified vaginal and testicular tumours. Radiography and ultrasonography demonstrated well-defined soft tissue masses. CTVT was the most prevalent urogenital neoplasm, highlighting the importance of combining clinical examination, imaging, cytology, and histopathology for accurate diagnosis and treatment evaluation.

title: Histopathological Analysis and Renal Toxicity of Silver Nanoparticles upon Frequent Oral Exposure in Wistar Rats
abstractText: Silver Nanoparticles (AgNPs) are the most widely produced engineered nanoparticles and account for more than 50% of global nanomaterial consumer products. Because of their small size, AgNPs can enter the human body through ingestion, inhalation, and skin contact. Kidneys, lungs, nervous system, and liver are organs prone to the accumulation of AgNPs and cause various histological changes as well as damage to organs. The objective of this study was to evaluate the renal toxicity induced by AgNPs after repeated oral exposure through pathomorphology and immunohistochemistry of kidneys in Wistar rats. Wistar rats (n=35) of either sex were randomly classified into two groups (treated, n=20; and control group, n=15). The control group of rats received normal feed and water, while test rats were given AgNPs in the form of suspension by oral gavaging at NOAEL dose (30 mg/kg b.wt.). On day 0, 5 rats from test group were weighed and euthanized, while at days 30th, 60th and 90th of the experiment, 5 rats from each control and test group were weighed and humanely euthanized to check pathomorphological changes of kidney. Histopathological changes were assessed using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) stain. For immunohistochemistry, at day 90th kidney tissue sections of treated rats were examined for the presence of antigen-antibody complexes using immunoperoxidase reaction to check histopathological changes. Pathomorphological studies revealed gross changes after 90 days of AgNPs exposure as compared to control group. Congestion and endothelial swelling in glomerular capillaries, focal infiltration of inflammatory cells in the glomeruli and in medullary area, cloudy swelling of the kidney tubular epithelium (KTE) which later progressed to coagulative necrosis were seen. Apoptotic figures like blebs were seen in the renal tubules. Proliferation of mesangial cells and expansion of mesangial matrix was seen at 60th and 90th day of experiment. Thus, AgNPs were responsible for in vivo renal damage.

title: Assessment of Feeding Practices Followed by Dairy Buffaloes Owners in Bhavnagar District of Gujarat State
abstractText: A field survey was conducted between March and May 2025 in the Bhavnagar district of Gujarat state to assess the feeding practices followed by dairy buffalo farmers. Using a multistage random sampling technique, six talukas (Talaja, Sihor, Palitana, Bhavnagar, Mahuva, and Umrala) were selected, with two villages from each taluka and ten respondents per village owning buffaloes yielding ≥8 kg milk/day. Data on 153 buffaloes from 120 farmers were collected through structured interviews and analysed. All farmers (100%) adopted stall-feeding, with none relying on grazing. A majority (77.50%) fed a combination of concentrate, green fodder, and dry fodder, while 21.67% used concentrate and dry fodder only, and 0.83% used concentrate with green fodder. Most farmers (92.50%) fed concentrates twice daily, primarily in dry form (61.67%), with 38.33% soaking before feeding. Roughage processing was rare, with only 7.50% and 4.17% practicing chaffing green and dry fodder, respectively, before feeding. Mineral supplementation was minimal (11.67%). Water was provided ad libitum, though frequency varied. Concentrate feeding during the dry period was reported by limited farmers (22.50%), while 72.50% offered pregnancy allowances and 74.17% provided extra feed and supplements to buffaloes post-calving. Identified gaps in the existing feeding practices were addressed with suitable recommendations.

title: Haemato-Biochemical Changes and Therapeutic Outcomes in Cerebral Babesiosis in Dogs
abstractText: Canine cerebral babesiosis is a rare, but life threatening neurological manifestation of Babesia gibsoni infection with scant documentation in India. The aim of the present study was to evaluate the clinical, haemato-biochemical changes with response to treatment in dogs with cerebral babesiosis (n=11). Cerebral babesiosis was initially suspected based on the presence of characteristic neurological signs and subsequently confirmed by microscopic examination of stained peripheral blood smears, and molecular confirmation by species-specific PCR targeting the 18S rRNA gene of Babesia gibsoni, which yielded the expected 670-bp amplicon. Eleven dogs diagnosed with cerebral babesiosis were treated with diminazene aceturate, doxycycline, enrofloxacin, metronidazole, and supportive medications. Clinical, haematological and serum biochemical parameters were assessed on days 0, 3, 7, 14 and 28 post-treatment. Neurological signs included ataxia, hind limb stiffness, paddling, opisthotonus, seizures, head pressing, stupor, circling, nystagmus, blindness and paraplegia, which mostly improved slowly after treatment. Haematological evaluation showed anaemia, leukocytosis and marked changes in the lymphocyte, eosinophil and monocyte profiles in the early phase. Haemoglobin and erythrocyte parameters improved progressively after therapy and leukocyte abnormalities progressively approached the values recorded in apparently healthy dogs. Serum biochemical analysis showed significant changes in albumin, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, direct bilirubin and BUN. High concentrations of ALT, ALP, bilirubin and BUN were observed at the beginning of the study and gradually decreased with treatment, while albumin concentration increased in the direction of the normal range. There were no significant differences in globulin, A/G ratio, creatinine, indirect bilirubin, glucose and magnesium. Results suggest cerebral babesiosis is associated with a poor prognosis despite intensive therapy, and combination chemotherapy with appropriate supportive care improved clinico-pathological and haemato-biochemical parameters and recovery of surviving dogs. Early diagnosis and treatment are thus still important to improve clinical outcomes.

title: Repair of Compound Tibiotarsus Fracture using Intramedullary Pinning in a Pigeon
abstractText: Tibio-tarsus bone is formed from a union of the tibia and the proximal row of tarsal bones during the embryonic growth (Suryawanshi et al., 2021). The biggest leg bone in birds, the tibiotarsus, is usually twice as long as the femur (Sreeranjini et al., 2013). The mineral content of avian bones is somewhat higher than that of human bones, which leads to an increased incidence of open fractures that are comminuted and include many sharp pieces that can be traumatic to the soft tissues that are surrounding the bone (Kumar et al., 2022). The frequent occurrence of fractures is attributed to the thin skin and comparatively low muscle mass that surround the bone. According to Wright et al. (2018), the mid-diaphyseal section accounts for the majority of tibiotarsal fractures, which account for 53% of cases. The proximal third and distal third of the tibiotarsal diaphysis are the sites of 22% and 13% of fractures, respectively. Wright et al. (2018) claimed that tibiotarsal fractures were frequently caused by a range of circumstances, such as maltreatment by the owner (22%), dropping from a perch (9%), and trauma triggered by an attack by a dog or cat (7%). Nevertheless, the etiology of the tibiotarsal fracture was not specified in 47% of the cases. According to Verma et al. (2018), avian fractures can be the result of either natural events, such as mid-air collisions or scuffles with other birds, or anthropogenic experiences, such as gunshot wounds, collisions with automobiles or fences, entrapment, or attacks by canines or cats. In both captive and untamed birds, bone fractures were a common occurrence. The current report delineates the successful surgical treatment of a compound tibiotarsus fracture in a pigeon through the use of intramedullary fixation with orthopaedic wire.

title: Etiopathological Study of Colisepticemia with Coinfection of Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza and Mycoplasma in Broilers
abstractText: The present study was conducted to detect Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI) and Mycoplasma in 30 broiler flocks (5 birds per flock) showing gross lesions of colisepticemia (Fibrinous pericarditis and perihepatitis) without any significant gross lesion in trachea and bronchi. The study comprised of flock wise mortality, gross and histopathological examination of colisepticemia and molecular identification from pooled sample of trachea for the presence of E. coli, LPAI, Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Mycoplasma synoviae. The mortality among 30 flocks varied between 0.32 and 6.75% with an average of 1.89%. Gross and histopathological lesions were predominantly found in liver, heart, spleen and lungs. All the 30 flocks were found positive for phoA gene of E. coli, whereas 5 (16.60%), 9 (30%) and 4 (13.30%) flocks were positive for H9N2 subtype of Avian influenza virus, i.e. LPAI, Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Mycoplasma synoviae, respectively. Findings of the present study confirmed the concurrent infection of colisepticemia with other primary pathogens such as LPAI, M. gallisepticum and M. synoviae, which indicate that Escherichia coli is a major secondary opportunistic pathogen in a respiratory disease complex of chicken.

title: Phytochemical Characterization and Antioxidant Potential of Cichorium intybus Root Extracts
abstractText: Cichorium intybus L. is a medicinal plant recognized for its rich phytochemical composition and diverse pharmacological properties. The present study comparatively evaluated the extraction yield, phytochemical composition, and antioxidant potential of aqueous, methanolic, and hydroethanolic (70%) root extracts of C. intybus. The extracts were analyzed for extraction yield, qualitative phytochemical constituents, total flavonoid content (TFC), total phenolic content (TPC), and nitric oxide (NO) radical scavenging activity. The aqueous extract exhibited the highest extraction yield (18.25 ± 0.56%), whereas the hydroethanolic extract showed the broadest phytochemical profile. Quantitative analysis demonstrated that the hydroethanolic extract contained the highest TFC (38.44 ± 0.33 mg QE/100 g DW) and TPC (250.75 ± 0.86 mg GAE/100 g DW). Consistently, this extract exhibited the strongest nitric oxide radical scavenging activity, with the lowest IC₅₀ value (261.83 µg/mL), indicating superior antioxidant potential. These findings suggest that hydroethanolic extraction is an efficient approach for recovering bioactive phytochemicals from C. intybus roots and highlight its potential as a natural source of antioxidant compounds for nutraceutical and pharmaceutical applications.

title: Clinical Assessment of Pain in Horses with Colic using Composite Pain Scale and Horse Grimace Scale
abstractText: The current study evaluated two pain assessment measures in horses with colic: (1) the Composite Pain Scale (CPS), which assesses overall clinical (behavioural and physiological) pain, and (2) the Horse Grimace Scale (HGS), which examines changes in pain-related facial expressions. A total of 30 horses with a clinical diagnosis (based on clinical signs) of colic were tested over four days of treatment. Pain evaluation was used to divide colic in horses into mild, moderate and severe pain groups according to severity. The control group consisted of eight clinically and apparently healthy horses. CPS scores differed significantly between pain groups (p < 0.01), with horses experiencing severe pain having the highest score, followed by moderate and mild pain. HGS scores were considerably higher (p < 0.01) in horses experiencing moderate to severe pain. Both pain scores in colic-affected horses decreased gradually throughout the therapy period. These findings imply that the CPS is an effective and objective tool for assessing and monitoring the degree of acute pain associated with equine colic. The HGS may provide further information on pain-related facial (expression) changes and can complement clinical pain assessment. These measures may support veterinarians in assessing pain severity, monitoring changes during treatment and improving pain management in horses with colic.

title: Risk Factors Analysis for Haemoparasitic Infections and Evaluation of Detection Methods for Ehrlichiosis in Dogs
abstractText: The frequency of occurrence of canine haemoparasitic diseases was analysed in relation to associated risk factors by examining the Leishman-stained thin blood smears of 400 dogs (pet 352 and stray 48) from the Ludhiana district of Punjab state, India. To compare the effectiveness of classic-immuno-molecular techniques, 50 samples suspected of ehrlichiosis were tested by buffy coat smear examination, Immuno-chromatographic lateral flow assay (LFA-Ec) and Polymerase chain reaction (Ec-PCR) based diagnosis by amplification of a fragment of the E. canis virB9. The occurrence of haemoparasites was 6.00% with the highest prevalence of B. gibsoni (3.75%), followed by H. canis (1.25%), E. canis (0.5%), B. canis (0.25%) and Trypanosoma evansi (0.25%) with higher prevalence of haemoparasites in stray dogs (8.33%) than pet dogs (5.68%). Exercise intolerance and fever were significantly (p≤0.01) associated with occurrence of haemoparasites. The kappa value revealed “slight” and “fair” strength of agreement for LFA-Ec & Ec-PCR with buffy coat smear examination. A sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 4.26% & 68.09% was observed respectively for LFA-Ec & Ec-PCR when compared with buffy coat smear examination. The complete sequence of the virB9 gene of E. canis showed the closest homology with the isolates obtained from the USA strain. This study underscores the importance of accurate diagnostic techniques and the influence of various risk factors on the prevalence of haemoparasitic diseases in dogs.

title: Therapeutic Efficacy of Allium sativum and Calendula officinalis against Secondary Otitis in Dogs
abstractText: Secondary otitis is a common inflammatory ear condition in dogs associated with bacterial and fungal infections. The increasing concern regarding antimicrobial resistance has encouraged the exploration of herbal alternatives with antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. The present study was undertaken to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of Allium sativum and Calendula officinalis infused oils against secondary otitis in dogs. Eighteen dogs with cytologically confirmed secondary otitis were randomly divided into three treatment groups (n=6 each). Six apparently healthy dogs were kept as the control group. Group G1 received Calendula officinalis infused oil, Group G2 received Allium sativum infused oil, and Group G3 received a combination of both infused oils topically 4-5 drops twice daily for 14 days. Clinical index score, yeast count, and bacterial load were evaluated on days 0, 7, and 14. Significant improvement in clinical and cytological parameters was observed in all treatment groups. The combination therapy (G3) showed the highest therapeutic efficacy with 92.11 % reduction in clinical score and 87.22 % reduction in yeast count by day 14 post-treatment, along with restoration of bacterial count to normal levels in all treated dogs. Group G1 showed better response than Group G2. The findings indicated that combined topical administration of both infused oils is an effective herbal therapy for secondary otitis in dogs.

title: Intraluminal Intestinal Obstruction due to a Retained Surgical Sponge in a Spayed Bitch
abstractText: A 4 year old female West Highland white terrier, weighing about 7.5 Kg was presented with a week-long history of persistent vomiting and anorexia. Barium contrast radiography showed brief accumulation of the agent outlining an oval structure, measuring 2.24 x 1.45 inches in the small intestines. Ultrasonography revealed a hypoechoic mass with a hyperechoic center in the cranial intestines. Surgical exploration disclosed an outpouching in the jejunum with a granulomatous reaction surrounding an intramural foreign body continuous with the lumen. The affected intestine was resected and anastomosed. Histopathology suggested the foreign body as a retained surgical sponge. On enquiry, the animal underwent an ovariohysterectomy a year ago. The dog recovered uneventfully with no post-operative complications.

title: QR Code-Integrated Standardization of Permanent Histological Slide Preparation: An Innovative Approach for Teaching Practical Histology
abstractText: Histological slides are essential tools for teaching and research in veterinary anatomy and histology. Standardized preparation of permanent slides across multiple domestic species, combined with modern digital integration, can enhance their educational and research utility. This study was aimed to standardize slide preparation and incorporate QR code-based digital access for improved visualization and learning. A total of 86 tissue samples were collected from buffalo (n=38), domestic fowl (n=20), dog (n=15), and goat (n=13). Representative tissues from major organs were fixed in 10% neutral buffered formalin and processed using routine histological techniques, including graded dehydration, clearing, and paraffin embedding. Sections of 4-6 μm thickness were cut using a rotary microtome, stained with hematoxylin and eosin, and permanently mounted with DPX. High-resolution photomicrographs were captured using a compound microscope equipped with a digital imaging system, and QR codes were generated and linked to the corresponding digital images for instant access via smart devices. The prepared slides demonstrated excellent preservation of tissue architecture, with clear cellular and structural details across all species. QR code integration enabled efficient digital cataloging, rapid retrieval, and enhanced visualization of histological features. The standardized protocol proved reliable and reproducible for permanent slide preparation in multiple domestic species, while the incorporation of QR code technology significantly improved accessibility and educational value.

title: Surgical Management of Concurrent Medial Patellar Luxation and Cranial Cruciate Ligament Rupture in a Chihuahua Crossbreed Dog
abstractText: A 4-year-old Chihuahua crossbreed dog was presented with chronic left hind limb lameness acutely exacerbated following a traumatic incident 45 days prior to presentation. Orthopedic examination revealed grade 3 medial patellar luxation with a shallow trochlear groove, tibial internal rotation, and a positive cranial drawer sign indicated concurrent cranial cruciate ligament rupture. Radiographic evaluation confirmed a shallow trochlear groove, internal tibial rotation, a fat pad sign indicating joint effusion, and mild osteoarthritis. Due to financial constraints, the owner declined advanced diagnostic imaging (arthroscopy or MRI) as well as tibial plateau leveling osteotomy. Surgical intervention was performed combining tibial tuberosity transposition with tension band wiring, trochlear wedge recession, and lateral fabellar extracapsular stabilization using 80 lbs nylon suture. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, with marked improvement in lameness and stifle stability at 12-day follow-up. This case demonstrates that combined extracapsular stabilization and patellar realignment can be a viable and cost-effective surgical approach for managing concurrent medial patellar luxation and cranial cruciate ligament rupture in small dog breeds when advanced osteotomy techniques are not feasible.

title: Haemato-Biochemical Changes in Dermatitis Associated with Penicillium spp. in Dogs
abstractText: Skin infection in dogs is classified as primary infection, caused by infectious organisms directly and secondary infections, which are augmented by underlying conditions that act as catalysts for infections such as bacterial or fungal infections. Among fungal infections, Penicillium is one of the largest genera. Penicillium species can cause allergies and both superficial and invasive infections. Keeping the above facts in view, the present research was undertaken to study the haemato-biochemical alterations in clinically affected dogs with Penicillium spp. associated dermatitis. A total of 200 dogs were selected for the study. Skin scraping samples were collected for culture and microscopic identification. Out of 200 dogs screened, 23 (11.5%) dogs were found positive for Penicillium-associated dermatitis based on skin scraping, Penicillium culture and identification. Penicillium-associated dermatitis in dogs revealed an increase in TLC, lymphocytes, eosinophils and total protein, and a decrease in serum zinc and copper concentration. On the basis of heamato-biochemical profile group T₁ showed better recovery. Twelve positive dogs, 6 each, treated with Tab. Terbinafine @ 30 mg/kg b.wt. (T1), and Tab. Itraconazole @ 10 mg/kg b.wt. (T2), PO, OD, for 21 days, with supportive therapy, resulted in normalization of these altered profiles by day 28 of treatment, at par with healthy control group, (T3, n=6). Basis of clinical recovery and haemato-biochemical analysis treatment Tab. Terbinafine showed better results from Penicillium-associated canine dermatitis.

title: Molecular Characterisation of Trefoil Factor 1 from Cases of Canine Mammary Tumour
abstractText: Canine mammary tumours (CMT) are among the most common neoplasms in female dogs and exhibit variable biological behaviour, necessitating the identification of reliable molecular biomarkers. Trefoil Factor 1 (TFF1) has been studied extensively in human cancers and has been found to be an important prognostic marker associated with tumour growth and progression. The present study was aimed to characterise TFF1 in canine mammary tumours tissues collected from clinical cases (n=10). Histopathological examination revealed diverse tumour patterns, including tubulopapillary carcinoma, carcinoma in situ, and stromal desmoplasia, indicating varying degrees of malignancy. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated variable cytoplasmic TFF1 expression in neoplastic epithelial cells, ranging from strong to weak immunoreactivity among different tumour subtypes, indicating heterogeneous protein expression within canine mammary tumours. At the molecular level, the canine TFF1 gene was successfully amplified, cloned and sequenced. Sequence analysis showed 100% nucleotide identity with the published canine TFF1 sequence, while phylogenetic analysis demonstrated a high degree of conservation among mammalian species, particularly within the Carnivora lineage, highlighting its evolutionary significance.

title: Use of Polyaxial Locking Plate and Rod Reconstruction in the Treatment of Tibial Diaphyseal Fractures in Dogs
abstractText: Clinical efficacy of the polyaxial locking plate (PAX) combined with intramedullary (IM) pinning - the plate-rod technique - was assessed in six dogs aged 6-28 months, irrespective of breed and sex, with mid-diaphyseal tibial fractures. Males predominated (83.33%), and road traffic accidents were the leading cause (83.33%) among these cases. Closed oblique fractures accounted for 66.66% of cases, the remainder being spiral. Surgery was performed at a mean of 4.83 ±0.83 days post-injury under a standardized anaesthetic protocol. A cranio-medial approach was used, and the PAX system’s ability to angle screws up to 15° from perpendicular appeared to provide stable fixation across fracture configurations. Fixation used 2.7 mm or 3.5 mm PAX plates combined with 1.8-3.0 mm IM pins. Radiographs on days 0, 15, 30, 60 and 90 tracked alignment, implant position, and healing. One case (23 kg, high activity level) showed transient implant bending. Lameness improved progressively, reaching grade I (normal weight-bearing) by day 60 in all six dogs, and radiographic union was achieved in all cases by day 90. The polyaxial plate’s limited-contact design supported early weight-bearing and reduced postoperative complications.

title: Evaluation of Different Vitrification Methods and Cryoprotectants on Viability of In Vitro Matured Buffalo Oocytes
abstractText: The developmental competence of buffalo oocytes is greatly influenced by the vitrification process and the cryoprotectants used during cryopreservation. The present study was undertaken to evaluate the effect of different cryoprotectants on the developmental potential of vitrified buffalo oocytes in terms of cleavage, and blastocyst formation. A total of 201 (18.3±0.8/session) buffalo ovaries were collected from the slaughterhouse in 11 sessions, and 447 (40.6±3.5/session) cumulus-oocyte complexes (COCs) were recovered from 663 aspirated follicles. Following in vitro maturation (IVM), 397 (36.1±3.5/session; 87.83%) oocytes attained maturity and were allocated to four experimental groups: Group I (fresh, non-vitrified control; n=198), Group II (Vitrogen vitrification; n=64), Group III (DMSO + EG vitrification; n=74), and Group IV (DMSO + EG + Sucrose vitrification; n=61). After warming and in vitro fertilisation (IVF), a total of 318 presumptive zygotes were cultured in vitro (IVC). Fresh oocytes exhibited superior developmental competence compared with vitrified oocytes. The cleavage rate was highest in the fresh control group, with 130 out of 198 presumptive zygotes (11.8±1.8; 63.23%) undergoing cleavage, whereas vitrified groups (Groups II, III, and IV) showed markedly lower cleavage rates of 11.61% (0.7±0.3), 11.97% (0.6±0.2), and 11.61% (0.5±0.2), respectively. Similarly, blastocyst formation was highest (n=15 BLs) in the fresh control group (8.09%; 1.4±0.3), in comparison to Groups II, III, and IV, 2.44% (0.2±0.1), 0.91% (0.09±0.8), and 1.52% (0.1±0.08), respectively. Although minor variations were observed among the results of different vitrification protocols, all vitrified groups demonstrated substantially reduced embryonic development compared with fresh oocytes.

title: Urological and Ultrasonographic Studies on Kidney Diseases in Dogs in Udaipur Region of Rajasthan

A total of 1,524 cases of dogs suffering from different ailments were registered at Veterinary Clinical Complex of College and Veterinary Polyclinic, Udaipur. title: Effects of Essential Oil Blend on Growth Performance, Carcass Traits and Blood Biochemical Profiles of Rainbow Rooster Chickens
abstractText: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of different levels of essential oil (thymol‑cinnamaldehyde-menthol 1:1:1) blend on the growth performance, carcass traits, blood biochemical profiles and gut health of chickens was undertaken on a total of 160-day-old mixed-sex Rainbow Rooster chicks. The chicks were randomly assigned to four experimental groups (T1 to T4), each comprising 40 chicks divided into five replicates of eight chicks. T1 (control) group received no growth promoters, while the T2 group was given Enromycin at 80 g/ton feed. The T3 and T4 groups received the oil blend at 100 and 200 mg/kg of feed, respectively. Body weight gain, feed consumption, and feed conversion ratio were monitored weekly. Blood samples were collected on day 42. Carcass traits were assessed at the end of the trial. Results showed that the essential oil blend and antibiotic-supplemented groups had significantly lower average daily feed intake and improved FCR compared to the control group. There were no significant effects on carcass traits. The serum cholesterol level was significantly lower in the groups supplemented with a blend of essential oils compared to the control group, whereas total protein, albumin and uric acid did not differ among dietary treatment groups. In conclusion, essential oil blend at 100 mg/kg diet could serve as viable alternatives to antimicrobials in poultry production.

title: Clinical and Haemato-Biochemical Alterations in Dogs Diagnosed with Demodicosis in Jaipur, Rajasthan
abstractText: Demodicosis is a common dermatological condition in dogs that produces characteristic cutaneous lesions and may also cause important haematological and biochemical alterations. This study was conducted to characterize the clinical signs, lesion distribution, and haemato-biochemical changes in demodicosis affected dogs. A total of 219 dogs with dermatological lesions were screened, out of which 30 were confirmed positive for demodicosis by standard skin-scraping examination and trichogram. Also, 10 apparently healthy dogs served as controls for the haemato-biochemical comparisons. The study revealed that alopecia, erythema, and erosions were observed in all affected dogs (100%), followed by papules (80%), hyperkeratosis (73.33%), pustules (53.33%), scars (50%), vesicles (40%), excoriation (23.33%), lichenification (20%), and hyperpigmentation (13.33%). The periocular region and back were the most frequently affected sites (93.33% each), followed by the abdomen (86.66%) and face and neck (83.33% each). The haemato-biochemical study revealed that affected dogs had lower mean haemoglobin and packed cell volume, higher total leucocyte counts, neutrophilia and eosinophilia, elevated ALT, AST, total protein, globulin, and glucose, and reduced albumin while compared to healthy dogs. These findings explains that canine demodicosis is associated with very specific patterns of skin lesions, systemic, haematological and biochemical alterations.
