title: Effects of Mineral Supplementation and Deworming on Improving Productive and Reproductive Performance of Jaffarabadi Buffaloes
abstractText: The present study was aimed to evaluate the impact of chelated mineral mixture and calcium supplementation combined with regular deworming on the productivity, reproductive performance, and economic returns of lactating Jaffarabadi buffaloes. The experiment involved 50 buffaloes of varying parities, managed by small and marginal farmers from the six different villages in Bagasara Taluka, Amreli District, Gujarat, over the period of 3 years (2020-23) under the Farmers FIRST Programme (FFP). Daily milk yield of the buffaloes prior to the intervention served as the control and milk yield data were collected monthly basis. The treatment group received a commercially available chelated mineral mixture @ 40 g and a calcium supplement at 50 mL/buffalo/day during the first 90 days of lactation, along with deworming at three-month intervals (Fenbendazole bolus 3g). Results showed a significant improvement in milk production in the treatment group, with average daily yields increasing from 7.16 litres (control) to 8.27 litres - a 15.64 % gain due to the intervention. Economic analysis revealed an additional gross return of ₹ 53.73 per buffalo per day. After accounting for input costs, farmers achieved an additional net return of ₹ 42.99 per buffalo per day, amounting to ₹ 12896 per buffalo annually, with a benefit-cost ratio (BCR) of 1.25. Farmers reported the intervention as practical and adoptable. An impact survey further showed that the technology was being adopted by neighbouring non-participant farmers, leading to increased milk yields and income. Overall, the intervention contributed to the socio-economic up-liftment of buffalo owners in the region.

title: Comprehensive Cardiac Assessment in Dogs using Electrocardiography, Echocardiography and Cardiac Biomarkers
abstractText: Cardiac diseases are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in dogs and require timely diagnosis for effective clinical management. A total of 52 dogs with clinical suspicion of cardiac disease were examined and compared with six apparently healthy control dogs at Veterinary Clinical Complex, Kamdhenu University, Navsari, Gujarat. Diagnosis was established using ECG and echocardiography and supported by haemato-biochemical analysis and assessment of cardiac troponin-I (cTnI) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) was the most prevalent cardiac disorder (46.15%), followed by mitral valve disease (MVD) (38.46%), pericardial effusion (11.53%), and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (3.84%). The most common clinical signs were exercise intolerance (92.30%), dyspnea (88.46%), and weakness (86.53%). ECG revealed atrial fibrillation (30.76%) and sinus tachycardia (25.00%) as the predominant rhythm abnormalities. Echocardiography demonstrated significant ventricular dilatation, increased E-point to septal separation, and reduced ejection fraction and fractional shortening in DCM, whereas MVD was characterized by marked left atrial enlargement and an increased left atrial-to-aortic root ratio. Haematological findings revealed mild anaemia, neutrophilia, and lymphopenia, while biochemical alterations were characterized by increased BUN and reduced serum albumin concentrations. Cardiac biomarkers showed marked diagnostic value, with elevated NT-proBNP concentrations and positive cTnI results in 70% of affected dogs. The findings indicate that ECG, echocardiography and cardiac biomarkers are valuable complementary tools for the accurate diagnosis and assessment of canine cardiac diseases.

title: Hospital Incidence and Clinico-Therapeutic Management of Trypanosomiasis in Horses
abstractText: Haemoprotozoal infection especially Trypanosoma evansi in horses has been found to be quite an ambiguity because they were regularly presented either as a carrier or with clinical signs of intermittent fever, peripheral edema, emaciation, urticaria with varying degree. In the present study, hospital incidence of trypanosomiasis was observed to be 17.78% (8/45) among horses presented with above signs. The disease was diagnosed by blood smear examination and PCR. The horses were successfully treated with diminazene aceturate along with supportive therapy and recovered within 5 days of treatment with normalization of altered haemato-biochemical profile.

title: Effects of Varying Levels of Shrimp Meal on Production Performance, Sensory Attributes, and Meat Quality of Broiler Chickens
abstractText: The study was aimed to evaluate the impact of different levels of shrimp meal inclusion on the growth performance, sensory attributes, and meat quality of broiler chickens. Three groups of 56 chicks each were randomly selected from a total of 168 day-old mixed-sex broiler chicks and divided into 7 replicates of 8 chicks. The experimental groups included SM1 (2.5% shrimp meal), SM2 (5% shrimp meal), and a control group fed a diet without shrimp meal. Body weight gain, feed intake, and feed conversion ratio were measured on days 0, 7, 14, 21, 28, and 35. At the end of the trial, muscle pH, water holding capacity, colour, flavour, tenderness, cooking loss and biochemical parameters were assessed. The study found that final body weights and average daily gain in SM2 group were significantly higher compared to control group and overall FCR showed better in SM2 group compared to SM1 and control groups. There were no significant effects on blood-biochemical profile, sensory qualities, excepting flavour, muscle pH and WHC value but there was significant difference in cooking loss among the treatments. The study findings show that incorporating up to 5% shrimp meal into a broiler diet primarily composed of maize and soybeans is safe and does not adversely impact the birds' performance.

title: Rectal Diverticulectomy for Obstipation Induced Rectal Diverticulum in a Cocker Spaniel Intact Male Dog
abstractText: Rectal diverticulum is a blind out-pouching of rectum through the overlying perineal muscle layers, occurring mostly in middle-aged intact male dogs (Saulnier-troff et al., 2008). This condition may occur alone, but mostly it occurs concurrently or as sequel to perineal hernia. The exact cause remains unclear, but it may develop from localized areas of weakness in the rectal wall, which may be either congenital or acquired (Mehrjerdi et al., 2013). If left untreated or inadvertently managed, rectal diverticulum can lead to fecal retention and impaction within the diverticular sac, resulting in impaired defecation and continuous straining, which may subsequently increase the risk of perineal herniation (Lalzawmliana et al., 2019). Various surgical approaches have been described for this condition, such as diverticulectomy, plication, and segmental resection and anastomosis through rectal pull through technique (Maji and Guha, 2012). Diverticulectomy via a lateral perineal approach has demonstrated successful clinical results among those techniques (Lalzawmliana et al., 2019). The present report describes the surgical management of rectal diverticulum via diverticulectomy in a Cocker Spaniel dog.

title: Efficacy of Ovsynch Protocol with Double Dose of GnRH in Postpartum Anestrus Mehsana Buffaloes
abstractText: The present study compared the efficacy of the Ovsynch and modified Ovsynch protocols in enhancing fertility in anestrus postpartum Mehsana buffaloes. Sixteen buffaloes were selected and randomly divided into two groups: Group I and Group II. Both groups were treated with the Ovsynch protocol, with a modification in the dose of GnRH in Group II, which received a double dose of GnRH, 20 μg (5 mL) buserelin acetate, instead of 10 μg (2.5 mL), intramuscularly. The buffaloes underwent FTAI at 12 to 24 h post-second buserelin acetate injection. The rate of induced estrus was recorded as 100 % in both groups. The estrus duration and conception rate were higher in Group II than in Group I (21±1.96 vs 20.25±1.94 h; 87.50% vs 75.00%, respectively). It is concluded that the double dose of GnRH analogue used in the Ovsynch protocol improved estrus duration and conception rates in postpartum anestrus Mehsana buffaloes, with equal estrus induction efficacy.

title: Comparative Effect of an Iron-based In-Pack Oxygen Scavenger on Lipid Oxidation, Proteolysis and Microbial Deterioration of Fresh Deboned Pork and Cooked Pork Nuggets Tray-Packaged in Food-Grade Polypropylene Trays under Refrigeration
abstractText: Active packaging using oxygen scavengers is an established strategy to improve the chilled shelf life of muscle foods, but quantitative data comparing its effect across product matrices in a common packaging system are limited. The present study compared the effect of a food-grade iron-based oxygen scavenger sachet (O-SORB U100, 2.5 g) on the oxidative, proteolytic and microbiological deterioration of two pork products with markedly different intrinsic properties - fresh deboned pork chunks (raw, intact muscle) and cooked emulsion-based pork nuggets - tray-packaged in food-grade polypropylene trays sealed with HDPE wrap and stored at 4±1 °C. The HDPE wrap film was selected based on its superior performance among four wrap films (LDPE, LLDPE, HDPE, PVC) screened in companion experiments. The oxygen scavenger reduced day-of-spoilage TBARS by 16 % in fresh chunks (HDPE pair, day 8) and 5-9 % in pork nuggets (HDPE pair, days 19-21), and reduced microbial counts by 0.45 log CFU/g in fresh chunks. In fresh chunks, the dominant deterioration mode was microbial; the scavenger lengthened shelf life by 3 days (from 5 to 8 days; +60 %). In pork nuggets, the dominant deterioration mode was oxidative; the scavenger lengthened shelf life by 4 days (from 19 to 23 days; +21 %). The HDPE-plus-iron-based-oxygen-scavenger system therefore represents a single, commercially scalable platform suitable for both raw and processed pork retail.

title: Molecular Characterization of Escherichia coli Associated Haemorrhagic Gastroenteritis and Concurrent Sepsis in Canine Population in Patna
abstractText: The present study was conducted to determine the molecular incidence of Escherichia coli-associated haemorrhagic gastroenteritis (HGE) and its concurrent occurrence with sepsis in canine clinical cases presented to the Veterinary Clinical Complex, Bihar Veterinary College, Patna. Screening of suspected cases was initially performed based on characteristic clinical symptoms, following which fecal samples were subjected to molecular confirmation using PCR. Of the 150 fecal samples examined, 71 (47.33%) were found positive for E. coli. Among the affected dogs, Mongrels exhibited the highest incidence (35.21%, n=25) of the PCR-confirmed cases. Age-wise younger dogs were more susceptible, with puppies aged 3-6 months showing the highest incidence at 45.07% (n=32). A sex-wise greater prevalence was noted in males (63.38%, n=45) compared to females. Additionally, among the 71 PCR-confirmed HGE cases, 42 dogs were positive for systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), yielding an overall SIRS occurrence of 59.2%. These findings highlight the significant involvement of E. coli in canine HGE and underscore its association with systemic inflammatory complications.

title: Haemato-Biochemical Effects of Silver Fluorophosphate in Long Bone Fracture Repair in Dogs
abstractText: The objective of this study was to evaluate haematological and biochemical changes with silver fluorophosphate supplementation in the repair of long bone fractures in dogs. In Group I (six dog), long bone fractures were immobilized using a locking compression plate (LCP), while in Group II (six dog) long bone fractures were immobilized using LCP along with additional use of silver fluorophosphate granules. The animals were fasted for 12 h, with water withheld for 6 h before surgery for anaesthesia. Routine antibiotics and analgesics were administered and owners were instructed on wound care and limited movement for minimum 20 days. Results of haemato-biochemical evaluation carried out between two groups at fortnightly intervals showed non-significant (p>0.05) differences in all the parameters between the two groups and between periods within the group, except packed cell volume, serum calcium and alkaline phosphatase levels, which while differed significantly (p<0.05) between periods, although within normal physiological range.

title: Cryoprotective Effects of Fulvic Acid on Buffalo Bull Spermatozoa: A Concentration-Dependent Response
abstractText: The present study was aimed to evaluate the effect of fulvic acid supplementation in Tris-fructose-yolk-glycerol (TFYG) extender on sperm quality attributes of buffalo bulls at successive stages of cryopreservation. Semen ejaculates (n=12) collected from healthy breeding bulls using an artificial vagina were split into four aliquots and extended with TFYG containing 0.00 (control), 0.50, 1.00 and 1.50 % (w/v) fulvic acid. The samples were processed, equilibrated and cryopreserved. Progressive sperm motility was evaluated at the post-dilution, pre-freeze and post-thaw stages, while viability, morphological abnormalities, plasma membrane integrity and acrosome integrity were assessed at the post-dilution and post-thaw stages. The response to fulvic acid was distinctly biphasic. Post-thaw sperm motility and plasma membrane integrity were significantly (p<0.01) higher with 1.50 and 1.00 % fulvic acid, and viability with 1.50 %, compared to the control, whereas 0.50 % fulvic acid consistently reduced sperm motility, viability and plasma membrane integrity below the control, the reduction being statistically significant for viability (p<0.05). The extender with 1.50 % fulvic acid also maintained significantly better acrosome integrity (p<0.05) and lower sperm abnormalities than the lower concentrations and control. The findings indicate that fulvic acid confers cryoprotection above a threshold concentration, below which it exerts the opposite effect, and that 1.50 % (w/v) is the most effective inclusion level for buffalo semen cryopreservation

title: Modulatory Effects of Tinospora cordifolia Supplementation on Haematological and Biochemical Indices in Periparturient Crossbred Cows
abstractText: The present study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation with Tinospora cordifolia stem powder on the haematological and biochemical indices of periparturient crossbred cows. Twelve clinically healthy advanced pregnant crossbred (HF × K) cows were randomly allocated into two groups (n=6 each). The control group received the routine farm ration, whereas the treatment group received Tinospora cordifolia stem powder at 6% of the total concentrate mixture in addition to the routine farm ration, from 30 days prepartum to 30 days postpartum. Blood samples were collected at predetermined intervals on days -30, -20, -10, -5 prepartum, on the day of calving (day 0) and days +5, +10, +20 and +30 postpartum for haematological and biochemical analyses. In the treatment group, supplementation significantly (p<0.05) improved erythrocytic indices, including total erythrocyte count, haemoglobin concentration and packed cell volume and enhanced leukocyte responses, particularly total leukocyte count and lymphocyte percentage, indicating improved immune competence. Biochemically, treatment group exhibited significantly (p<0.05) lower blood glucose and non‑esterified fatty acid concentrations, suggesting improved metabolic adaptation and energy balance. Furthermore, serum total protein and albumin concentrations were significantly (p<0.05) higher in the treatment group, whereas globulin concentration remained comparable between two groups. These findings demonstrate that dietary Tinospora cordifolia supplementation may promote haematological stability, metabolic homeostasis and immune function, highlighting its potential as a natural phytogenic feed supplement for improving the health and physiological status of periparturient dairy cows.

title: Evaluation of Centrifuged Egg Yolk Extender with L-Methionine for Improving Cryosurvival of Kankrej Bull Spermatozoa
abstractText: The present study was undertaken to evaluate the effect of a centrifuged Tris-fructose egg yolk glycerol (TFEYG) extender supplemented with L-methionine on post-dilution and post-thaw semen quality, oxidative stress, and enzymatic activity in Kankrej bull semen. Eighteen ejaculates collected from three healthy, sexually mature Kankrej bulls were processed using three extender formulations: conventional TFEYG (Group I), centrifuged TFEYG (Group II), and centrifuged TFEYG supplemented with 2.5 mM L-methionine (Group III). Semen quality was assessed in terms of individual sperm motility, viability, abnormalities, hypo-osmotic swelling test (HOST)-reacted sperm, malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) at the post-dilution and post-thaw stages. Cryopreservation reduced semen quality in all treatment groups; however, semen extended with centrifuged TFEYG, particularly when supplemented with L-methionine, retained significantly (p<0.05) higher sperm motility, viability, and HOST‑reacted sperm, along with significantly lower sperm abnormalities than the conventional extender. The most favourable postthaw semen characteristics were consistently observed in Group III. Although MDA, SOD, and ALT values were not significantly affected by the treatments, post‑thaw AST activity was significantly lower in the L‑methionine‑supplemented group, indicating reduced membrane damage, while the group also showed lower MDA and higher SOD values after thawing. The results suggest that removal of deleterious egg yolk components through centrifugation, together with the antioxidant action of L‑methionine, improved the ability of spermatozoa to withstand cryopreservation. Supplementation of a centrifuged TFEYG extender with 2.5 mM L‑methionine can therefore be considered a useful approach for improving the post‑thaw quality of Kankrej bull semen.

title: Modulation of Metabolic and Oxidative Stress Biomarkers and Cortisol by Dietary Tinospora cordifolia Supplementation in Twin-Bearing Periparturient Surti Goats
abstractText: The present study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation of Tinospora cordifolia (Guduchi) on metabolic indices, oxidative stress biomarkers and cortisol concentration in twin-bearing periparturient Surti goats. Twelve clinically healthy advanced pregnant Surti goats carrying twin fetuses were randomly allocated into two groups (n=6 each). The control group received a routine diet, whereas, the treatment group received the routine diet supplemented with Tinospora cordifolia stem powder at 6% of the total concentrate mixture from 30 days before to 30 days after kidding. Blood samples were collected at regular intervals from day −30 prepartum to day +30 postpartum for analyses of metabolic and oxidative stress biomarkers and cortisol. Tinospora cordifolia supplementation significantly (p<0.05) increased blood glucose, serum albumin, calcium, superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activities, with reduced AST, malondialdehyde (MDA) and cortisol concentrations during critical stages of the periparturient period. Although serum total protein, ALT and creatinine did not differ significantly between the groups and supplemented goats consistently exhibited numerically favourable values. The findings demonstrate that Tinospora cordifolia supplementation may improve metabolic adaptation, strengthen antioxidant defence and alleviate oxidative and endocrine stress during the periparturient period, suggesting its potential as a natural phytogenic feed additive for enhancing the health and physiological resilience of transition dairy goats.

title: Diagnostic Efficacy of White Side Test and Endometrial Cytology for Detection of Endometritis in Repeat Breeding Mehsana Buffaloes of Banaskantha District, Gujarat
abstractText: This study evaluated the diagnostic efficacy of the Whiteside test and endometrial cytology for detecting endometritis in repeat-breeding Mehsana buffaloes. A total of 112 repeat-breeding Mehsana buffaloes from Banaskantha District, Gujarat, were screened for endometritis during estrus. Cervico-vaginal mucus samples were tested using the Whiteside test, and endometrial cytological samples were collected with a cytobrush and stained with Field's stain. Buffaloes with ≥8% polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs) in endometrial cytology were considered positive for endometritis. The Whiteside test detected endometritis in 26 of 112 buffaloes (23.21%), whereas endometrial cytology identified 35 positive cases (31.25%). The relative diagnostic efficacy of the Whiteside test was 74.28% compared with endometrial cytology. Among WST-positive buffaloes, 42.31% exhibited mild, 34.61% moderate, and 23.08% severe endometritis. The mean PMN percentage was significantly higher (p<0.05) in buffaloes with endometritis (11.04±2.13%) than in healthy buffaloes (2.50±1.65%). Endometrial cytology detected more subclinical endometritis cases than the Whiteside test. Endometrial cytology technique proved to be a more sensitive and reliable method for detecting subclinical endometritis in repeat breeding Mehsana buffaloes, whereas the White side test served as a rapid, economical, and practical field screening tool. The combined application of both techniques can facilitate early diagnosis and improve reproductive management under field conditions.

title: Evaluation of Alternatives to Conventional Egg Yolk Extender for Cryopreservation of Kankrej Bull Semen
abstractText: Demand for alternative of egg yolk in freezing extenders have increased in recent years due to variability in egg yolk composition, risk of microbial contamination and presence of steroid hormones. The alternative to egg yolk-based extender can be extender prepared using centrifuged egg yolk (cEY) and liposome based extender (Liposome). Therefore, this study was designed to compare cEY and Liposome with universal EY for evaluation of various physical and biochemical parameters of 18 ejaculates collected from Kankrej bull (n=3). Results revealed that at the post-thawed (PT) stage, individual sperm motility, HOST reactive sperm, and sperm viability were significantly higher (p<0.05) in liposome based extender compared to the EY extender. Malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), aspartate amino transaminase (AST) and alanine amino transaminase (ALT) were estimated from seminal plasma at post‑dilution and post‑thaw stages of cryopreservation. The Liposome based extender and cEY extender showed a significant (p<0.05) decrease in MDA, AST and ALT level, whereas, SOD level non‑significant as compared to the EY extender.

title: Gross Morphometry of Large Intestine in Postnatal Age Groups of Indian Domestic Pig (Sus scrofa domesticus)
abstractText: The present study on gross morphometry of large intestine was conducted on different postnatal age groups (Group I piglets, 0-4 weeks, Group II weaners, 4-10 weeks and Group III adults, above 10 weeks, n=6 each) of Indian domestic pig. The large intestine of pig grossly appeared as a complex sacculated tube with caecum, colon and rectum attached to the dorsal wall of the abdominal cavity. The gross morphometrical observations revealed a significant increase in the length and diameter of all the segments of large intestine with advancing age. The total length of the large intestine increased from 107.58±11.27 cm in Group-I to 379.26±23.97 cm in Group-III. The length and diameters of the caecum increased significantly with age. The ascending colon showed characteristic centripetal and centrifugal turns. The total length of ascending colon increased from 80.53±10.28 cm in Group I to 164.97±8.48 cm in Group II and 287.83±20.67 cm in Group III. Similarly, significant (p<0.05) increase in the length and diameter of the transverse colon, descending colon and rectum were observed during postnatal growth. Among the colonic segments, the ascending colon showed the greatest length, whereas the rectum exhibited the greatest diameter in adult animals. The length of ascending colon and the diameter of rectum increased significantly (p<0.05) from Group I to Group III.

Prevalence and genetic variants of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in malaria-endemic communities along the Lake Victoria basin, Kenya
abstractText: Abstract Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, a common X-linked disorder in malaria-endemic regions, can cause haemolysis following primaquine treatment. Primaquine is vital for eliminating P. vivax , P. ovale hypnozoites, and P. falciparum gametocytes. Despite increasing non- falciparum malaria and artemisinin-resistant P. falciparum in Sub-Saharan Africa, primaquine uptake remains limited due to safety concerns in G6PD-deficient individuals. We assessed G6PD deficiency prevalence and its association with Plasmodium infections among 1661 individuals from five communities around Lake Victoria in Homa Bay County, Kenya. G6PD activity was measured using the Dojindo G6PD Assay Kit-WST, with deficiency defined as < 30% of the adjusted male median activity. Selected samples were genotyped for G202A, A376G, A542T, G680T, and T968C. Associations with Plasmodium infection and clinical attributes were analysed using ordinal logistic regression. Overall G6PD deficiency prevalence was 6.8% ( n = 113): 9.0% (69/765) in males and 4.9% (44/896) in females. G6PD deficiency was primarily explained by the G202A variant (G6PD A-/Asahi). Of 104 G6PD-deficient individuals genotyped, 66 were hemizygous, 26 homozygous, and 7 heterozygous for G6PD A- or Asahi variants. Whole gene sequencing further revealed G6PD Sibari (A634G) in a deficient male. G6PD deficiency did not protect against Plasmodium infection, however microscopic infections were associated with living in communities with higher parasite prevalence, male sex, young age, severe anaemia, and bed net disuse.

Application of Multidisciplinary Collaborative Teaching Based on Integrative Medicine in Thoracic Tumor Surgery Education
abstractText: AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of a multidisciplinary collaborative teaching model based on integrative medicine in thoracic tumor surgery education. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included sixty-one clinical interns who underwent training in the Department of Thoracic Disease Diagnosis and Treatment Center at The Third Affiliated Hospital of Jiaxing University (Zhejiang Rongjun Hospital) from March 2022 to March 2025. Based on the implementation period of the teaching model, participants were assigned to a control group (n = 30) or an observation group (n = 31). The control group received traditional teaching, whereas the observation group received multidisciplinary collaborative teaching based on integrative medicine, including multidisciplinary team (MDT) case discussions, scenario-based simulation, and simulated surgical skills training. Both groups underwent 3 months of training. After training, the theoretical knowledge assessment scores, comprehensive clinical competence (Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX) assessment, including dimensions such as medical history taking and case analysis, clinical reasoning and judgment, doctor-patient communication, and Organization/Efficiency), operational skills (operational standardization, teamwork, instrument proficiency, and mastery of basic surgical skills), and teaching satisfaction were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: After training, the observation group achieved significantly higher theoretical knowledge scores than the control group (p < 0.05). For comprehensive clinical skills, the observation group scored significantly higher in history taking and case analysis, clinical reasoning and judgment, and Organization/Efficiency (p < 0.05), whereas no significant difference was observed in doctor-patient communication (p = 0.402). Regarding operational skills, the observation group performed significantly better in operational standardization, teamwork, and instrument proficiency (all p < 0.05), while basic skills mastery did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.262). Teaching satisfaction scores for teaching methods, teaching content, learning enthusiasm, and overall satisfaction were significantly higher in the observation group (all p < 0.05), whereas no significant differences were found in effectiveness or practicality (all p > 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Multidisciplinary collaborative teaching based on integrative medicine was associated with improved theoretical knowledge, selected aspects of clinical competence (history taking and case analysis, clinical reasoning and judgment, Organization/Efficiency), certain operational skills (operation standardization, teamwork, and instrument proficiency), and higher teaching satisfaction. However, improvements were not observed across all competency domains. This teaching model may have value in standardized thoracic oncology training, although prospective studies are needed for further validation.

PLANTAS MEDICINAIS E FITOTERÁPICOS NA SAÚDE REPRODUTIVA DA MULHER: REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA
abstractText: Esse artigo buscou identificar e analisar as produções científicas brasileiras sobre o uso de plantas medicinais e fitoterápicos na saúde reprodutiva da mulher. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, realizada entre julho e outubro de 2025 nas bases PubMed, SciELO, ScienceDirect e Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde, com os descritores “Plantas Medicinais”, “Fitoterapia” e “Saúde Reprodutiva da Mulher”. Foram incluídos artigos publicados entre 2020 e 2025, em inglês, espanhol ou português. Seis artigos compuseram a amostra final, analisados quanto aos objetivos, ao tipo de estudo e aos resultados. Os estudos abordaram espécies como Curcuma longa, Allium sativum, Anethum graveolens, Foeniculum vulgare e Vitex agnus-castus no manejo da endometriose, da dismenorreia, da síndrome pré-menstrual, de infecções ginecológicas, do climatério e da menopausa, além dos riscos na gestação. Observaram-se efeitos anti-inflamatórios e antioxidantes e alívio de sintomas, mas também risco de reações adversas, interações medicamentosas, efeitos embriotóxicos e déficit de conhecimento dos profissionais de saúde. Conclui-se que a fitoterapia é uma alternativa acessível e potencialmente eficaz para o cuidado da mulher ao longo do ciclo de vida, porém seu uso exige orientação profissional, padronização dos extratos e mais estudos clínicos que comprovem sua eficácia e segurança.

Revisiting the Dunne Diagram: Seasonal Variation and Spatial Pattern of Runoff Components
abstractText: Abstract The classic Dunne Diagram qualitatively illustrates how atmospheric conditions, soil, and topography shape runoff generation mechanisms under long-term average conditions. This study revisits the diagram using a novel theoretical framework that unifies infiltration excess and saturation excess runoff into a continuous scheme governed by dynamic soil moisture variations across catchments. The framework captures the spatial and temporal transitions between runoff mechanisms. Using observational data from 600 natural catchments across diverse US atmospheric conditions and landscapes, we develop a data-driven, quantitative reinterpretation of the Dunne Diagram based on multiannual catchment behavior, and further examine runoff generation mechanisms at seasonal timescale. At the mean annual scale, saturation excess runoff dominates the West Coast and Eastern United States, infiltration excess runoff prevails in central regions, and baseflow dominates the Western interior and Appalachian areas. In the western United States, both saturation- and infiltration-excess runoff exhibit strong seasonality, closely following the precipitation patterns along the West Coast. Individual catchments show seasonal switching and coexistence of dominant runoff generation mechanisms. The Unified Scheme for Modeling Saturation and Infiltration Excess Runoff (URSSIE) model broadly reproduces the general pattern of the Dunne Diagram and provides quantitative support for the Dunne Diagram. This approach enhances the understanding of runoff processes and improves hydrologic modeling at catchment scales, with important implications for flood forecasting and water resource management in complex or changing hydrologic regimes.

title: The effect of a one-session slow breathing exercise on emotional reactivity, heart rate, and blood pressure in alexithymic vs. non-alexithymic individuals
FATORES OCUPACIONAIS ASSOCIADOS AO ESTRESSE E À ANSIEDADE NA ENFERMAGEM DE URGÊNCIA E EMERGÊNCIA NO BRASIL: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA
abstractText: Profissionais de enfermagem que atuam em serviços de urgência e emergência estão expostos a demandas imprevisíveis, pressão temporal e situações críticas, condições relacionadas ao estresse e à ansiedade. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar a produção científica brasileira sobre esses fenômenos, identificando fatores ocupacionais relacionados e estratégias de prevenção e suporte descritas na literatura. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa, de caráter descritivo-analítico, com buscas no PubMed e na Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde (BVS), abrangendo as bases LILACS e BDENF. Foram considerados estudos primários publicados entre 2021 e 2026, realizados no Brasil com profissionais de enfermagem atuantes em serviços de urgência e emergência. Foram identificados 189 registros provenientes das bases de dados. Após a remoção de 14 duplicatas, a triagem de títulos e resumos e a avaliação dos textos completos disponíveis, foram incluídos 23 estudos, publicados em 23 artigos. Destes, 12 foram classificados como transversais e 11 como qualitativos, com predominância de pesquisas nas regiões Sudeste e Sul. A prevalência de transtornos mentais comuns variou de 15,3% a 42,9%. Em um pronto-socorro, 38,6% dos profissionais apresentaram sintomas de estresse de moderados a extremamente graves e 29,5% apresentaram sintomas de ansiedade; em uma Unidade de Pronto Atendimento, 33,3% dos participantes apresentaram sintomas de ansiedade. Entre os fatores ocupacionais identificados, destacaram-se a sobrecarga de trabalho, o déficit de pessoal, a escassez de materiais e equipamentos de proteção, a violência ocupacional, a exposição à morte e a situações críticas, as relações de trabalho, o apoio da gestão, os múltiplos vínculos empregatícios e as condições relacionadas à pandemia de COVID-19. Nenhum dos estudos brasileiros incluídos avaliou intervenções. As estratégias identificadas compreenderam formas de enfrentamento relatadas pelos profissionais, ações institucionais não avaliadas quanto à efetividade e recomendações dos autores. Como contribuição técnico-educativa, elaborou-se a Matriz dos Três Tempos, que organiza possibilidades de prevenção antes, durante e após o plantão. Conclui-se que a prevenção do estresse e da ansiedade requer medidas voltadas às condições organizacionais e ao suporte institucional, bem como pesquisas que avaliem intervenções no contexto brasileiro.

title: Reducing Sampling Effort for Mapping Air Pollution: A Two-Stage Framework
abstractText: Abstract Mobile monitoring is essential for resolving intraurban air pollution gradients, yet its scalability is constrained by the intensive sampling required to produce stable concentration maps. Here, we develop a screen-and-target two-stage framework to help reduce the effort of mapping hyperlocal air pollution. Using large mobile-monitoring data sets from Shenzhen and Macau, we combined spatially constrained segmentation models with land-use machine learning to evaluate how sampling effort affects air pollution mapping stability. Mean NO2 higher-lower (binary) concentration zone classification agreement first exceeded 80% at 3% of randomly sampled observations in Shenzhen and 15% in Macau. Random selection of whole measurement days required more effort for the same agreement level: 27.7% of observations (8 days) in Macau and 22.6% (30 days) in Shenzhen. Land-use machine learning achieved 80% of the total reduction in prediction error with 25–36% road-network coverage across pollutants, but errors remained high in large unsampled areas. Under the same sampling effort, the screen-and-target strategy reduced road-segment NO2 estimation error by 18–32% relative to conventional uniform sampling, whereas its zone maps improved mainly at low effort (≤20% of the campaign effort). These findings can guide resource-efficient sampling strategies for mapping and mitigation of air pollution in cities.

ANALISIS STRATEGI KESANTUNAN BERBAHASA DALAM ANIME SHIROKUMA CAFE
abstractText: ABSTRACT Politeness in Japanese communication is essential for maintaining social harmony because language choices are influenced by social norms, interpersonal relationships, status, and communicative situations. Understanding how these factors shape speech acts is important for explaining the relationship between Japanese cultural values and linguistic politeness. This study aims to identify the types of directive speech acts and analyze the influence of social norms and interpersonal relationships on politeness in episodes 1–20 of the anime Shirokuma Cafe. This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, using character utterances in the anime as the data source. Data were collected through observation and note-taking techniques, then identified, classified according to the types of directive speech acts, and analyzed by considering their communicative contexts. Searle's theory was used to classify directive speech acts, while Ide's concept of wakimae served as the main framework for explaining how language use reflects social norms and social roles. Brown and Levinson's politeness theory was used as a complementary framework to examine politeness strategies related to face. The findings reveal 210 directive speech act data, consisting of 30 commands, 62 requests, 39 invitations, 46 suggestions or pieces of advice, and 33 prohibitions. The results indicate that the choice of directive forms and politeness strategies is influenced by interpersonal closeness, social status, social roles, and communicative situations. The integration of wakimae and Brown and Levinson's politeness theory provides a broader analytical perspective by connecting culturally determined social expectations with individual face-oriented strategies. This integration constitutes the main contribution of the study, demonstrating that Japanese politeness in Shirokuma Cafe is not merely determined by linguistic expressions but also reflects the interaction between social norms, interpersonal relationships, and contextual language choices. The study concludes that politeness in the anime is context-dependent and reflects the relationship between Japanese social norms and linguistic politeness strategies. ABSTRAK Kesantunan berbahasa dalam bahasa Jepang tidak hanya ditentukan oleh pilihan bentuk bahasa, tetapi juga dipengaruhi oleh norma sosial, status, hubungan antarpeserta tutur, dan situasi komunikasi. Pemahaman terhadap kesantunan tersebut penting untuk menjelaskan bagaimana penutur menyesuaikan tindak tutur dengan tuntutan sosial dan hubungan interpersonal dalam interaksi sehari-hari. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi jenis tindak tutur direktif serta menganalisis pengaruh norma dan hubungan sosial terhadap kesantunan berbahasa dalam anime Shirokuma Cafe episode 1–20. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan sumber data berupa tuturan tokoh dalam anime tersebut. Data dikumpulkan melalui teknik simak dan catat, kemudian diidentifikasi, diklasifikasikan berdasarkan jenis tindak tutur direktif, dan dianalisis dengan mempertimbangkan konteks tuturan. Klasifikasi tindak tutur direktif mengacu pada teori Searle, sedangkan teori wakimae dari Ide digunakan untuk menganalisis penyesuaian bahasa terhadap norma dan peran sosial. Teori kesantunan Brown dan Levinson digunakan sebagai pendukung untuk mengidentifikasi strategi kesantunan berdasarkan konsep muka (face). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan terdapat 210 data tindak tutur direktif, yang terdiri atas 30 perintah, 62 permintaan, 39 ajakan, 46 saran atau nasihat, dan 33 larangan. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa pemilihan bentuk direktif dan strategi kesantunan dipengaruhi oleh kedekatan antarpenutur, status, peran sosial, dan situasi komunikasi. Strategi bald on record, positive politeness, negative politeness, dan off record memperlihatkan variasi penyampaian direktif secara langsung, akrab, berhati-hati, atau tidak langsung. Kontribusi utama penelitian ini terletak pada integrasi konsep wakimae dari Ide dan teori kesantunan Brown dan Levinson untuk menjelaskan kesantunan berbahasa dari dua perspektif yang saling melengkapi, yaitu kepatuhan terhadap norma dan peran sosial serta strategi pengelolaan hubungan interpersonal. Integrasi tersebut memberikan pemahaman yang lebih menyeluruh mengenai bagaimana tindak tutur direktif disesuaikan dengan konteks sosial dalam komunikasi bahasa Jepang. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa kesantunan berbahasa dalam anime tersebut bersifat kontekstual dan mencerminkan keterkaitan antara norma sosial Jepang dan pilihan strategi berbahasa.

title: Language, Artificial Intelligence and Teacher Education: Bridging the Linguistic Gap
abstractText: Language difference can limit participation and understanding in multilingual classrooms, particularly where the language of instruction differs from learners’ home language. This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can support teacher education in addressing language barriers in multilingual Nigerian classrooms. Specifically, it explores the use of AI for translation, language practice, individualised learning and the development of multilingual teaching resources. This study is guided by a conceptual framework drawing on relevant literature on language education, AI, teacher education and Nigerian language policies. The research design was qualitative and conceptual review using secondary data sources on artificial intelligence, language education, multilingualism, teacher education and Nigerian indigenous languages. A thematic review of journal papers, research articles, policy papers and other contemporary writings was undertaken, with particular attention given to data sources published recently in Nigerian literature. The findings indicates that AI tools can improve access to learning materials, support language practice and promote communication across languages. However, their effectiveness depends on the availability of reliable digital language resources, the accuracy of AI-generated content and teachers’ digital literacy. The limited representation of Nigerian indigenous languages in digital resources remain a major challenge. This work concludes that AI can promote more inclusive multilingual education when used to support, rather than replace, teachers. It recommends strengthening teachers’ digital skills, promoting collaboration among linguists, language educators and technology developers, and investing in digital resources for Nigerian indigenous languages.

When Standard Answers Become Shackles: The Impact of Social Media Experience Substitution on Individual Decision-Making Autonomy
abstractText: Individuals are now sharing their experiences through social media posts in order to make decisions during the digital media age. This practice offers convenient access to information but might hinder independent thinking and decision-making autonomy. Experience substitution is defined as people substituting their own trial-and-error process with others' experiences. Based on information dependency theory, social comparison theory, and the availability heuristic, this paper investigates how social media information dependency influences decision-making autonomy and if critical thinking acts as a buffer between them. Through a questionnaire survey among 21 social media users (aged 15 – 22), the research finds that over 85% of the respondents actively search for others' experiences prior to making decisions; and over 90% of the respondents feel self-doubt whenever they have different experiences than those portrayed in mainstream narratives on social media. These results verify the presence of the experience substitution phenomenon, and show that critical thinking buffers the negative impact of social media information dependency upon decision-making autonomy.

title: Peer Effects in Labor Market Training
abstractText: This paper shows that group composition shapes the effectiveness of labor market training programs for jobseekers. Using rich administrative data from Germany and a novel measure of employability, I find that participants benefit from greater average exposure to highly employable peers through increased long-term employment and earnings. The effects vary significantly by own employability: jobseekers with a low employability experience larger long-term gains, whereas highly employable individuals benefit primarily in the short term through higher entry wages. An analysis of mechanisms suggests that within-group competition in job search attenuates part of the positive effects that operate through knowledge spillovers.

Theoretical Investigation of Protonated Cyanogen Formation in the Interstellar Medium: Energetics and Spectroscopy
abstractText: Protonated cyanogen (NCCNH+) has been detected in the interstellar medium toward the cold dark clouds TMC-1 and L483, as well as in the prestellar core L1544. In the present work, the formation of NCCNH+ has been discussed with the help of molecules that are primarily detected in the interstellar medium. This study explores the formation mechanisms of NCCNH+ using Density Functional Theory (DFT) at the UB3LYP-(D3-BJ)/aug-cc-pVTZ level of theory, coupled with high-accuracy CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVQZ single-point energy calculations. The radical-radical and ion-molecule interactions were studied to explore the possibility of protonated cyanogen formation. The reaction of two CN radicals has been proposed for the formation of NCCN which further reacts with pre-detected protonated molecules to form the protonated form of cyanogen (NCCNH+) in the gas phase. All reactions were found to be barrierless and exothermic, with the calculated thermochemical parameters indicating thermodynamic favorability under the adopted computational conditions. Spectroscopic properties, particularly infrared and electronic spectra, were analyzed to characterize the protonated species and provide reference data for laboratory and astronomical studies.

title: The Geometric Deformation of Curved $L_\infty$ Algebras and Lie Algebroids
abstractText: While $L_\infty$ algebras are fundamental structures in differential geometry and mathematical physics, the geometric information encoded in such structures is often implicit. We address the following question: What constitutes a geometrically meaningful deformation of an $L_\infty$ algebra arising from vector bundles, and how can such deformations classify new geometric invariants? Inspired by nonabelian extension theory of Lie algebras, we define geometric deformations of curved $L_\infty$ algebras constructed from a vector bundle $V\to M$, and demonstrate that such deformations uniquely correspond to Lie algebroid structures on $V$. Explicit computations reveal that a representative of the first Atiyah-Chern class is exact in the total Weil complex, with its primitive representing the modular class in Lie algebroid cohomology. In the case of action Lie algebroids, the leading-order Atiyah-Chern classes correspond to the equivariant Chern characters. Applications to BV theories show that the geometric deformations naturally generate Poisson sigma models. These results provide a coherent framework for deriving field theories from geometric deformations of $L_\infty$ algebras.

title: Evaluating behavioural responses of macropods to drones
abstractText: Context Wildlife monitoring is a crucial component of conservation management, and drones are an increasingly important tool for wildlife surveys. The response of wildlife to drone activities can vary depending on various factors, hence, the development of site- and species-specific protocols for drone-survey methods should be prioritised. Aims In this study, we aimed to evaluate the behavioural responses of two large terrestrial mammals from Tasmania, Australia – Bennett’s wallaby (Notamacropus rufogriseus) and Forester kangaroo (Macropus giganteus tasmaniensis) – towards a drone, with the goal of determining the feasibility of deploying drones for population monitoring of these species in their natural habitats. Methods We investigated the impacts of drone presence on Bennett’s wallaby and Forester kangaroo using a commercial quadcopter model. Individuals were observed under controlled drone approaches conducted at six flight altitudes, and behavioural responses were classified as undisturbed, vigilant or fled based on direct observation and video analysis. Key results We found that both macropod species showed increasing behavioural responses to the drone, including evasion, at lower flight altitudes and higher drone noise levels, particularly at 40 m above ground level (AGL) and below. At lower sound levels (48 dB and below, corresponding to flight altitudes above 50 m AGL), animals’ responses were minimal. These results indicate that drone-based surveys of Forester kangaroos and Bennett’s wallabies can be conducted with minimal disturbance when appropriate operational parameters are applied. Conclusions Our findings support the adoption of flight altitudes of 40–60 m AGL as a general guideline for reducing behavioural disturbance during drone-based monitoring of macropods under conditions similar to those examined in this study. These findings highlight the potential for drone-based monitoring of macropods with minimal behavioural disturbance when appropriate flight parameters are applied. Implications Our study has established fundamental information on the behavioural responses of Forester kangaroos and Bennett’s wallabies to drone operations, helping to identify flight parameters that can minimise disturbance during wildlife surveys. These findings can inform the development of drone-based monitoring protocols for macropods in Tasmania and provide a basis for further evaluation of species-specific responses to drone operations.

title: Kondratiev spaces of fractional smoothness via refined localization spaces
abstractText: In this paper, we introduce Kondratiev spaces of fractional smoothness based on their close relation to refined localization spaces. Moreover, we investigate relations to other approaches leading to extensions of the scale of Kondratiev spaces with integer order of smoothness, based on complex interpolation, and give further results for complex interpolation of those function spaces. The results are first established on complements of arbitrary closed Lebesgue null sets and then transferred to domains of polyhedral type. Finally, as an application, we will study Sobolev-type embeddings.

title: Traction Force Dynamics During Patient-Derived Glioblastoma Neurosphere Invasion in 3D Matrigel
abstractText: Abstract Purpose Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor with a 5-year survival rate below 7%. Poor outcomes are driven in part by diffuse invasion into surrounding brain tissue, which limits complete surgical resection and promotes recurrence. Improved therapies require a quantitative understanding of the mechanics of GBM invasion. Methods Patient-derived GBM neurospheres were embedded in Matrigel and analyzed using live imaging, three-dimensional traction force microscopy (3D TFM), and targeted cytoskeletal perturbations. Results Invading GBM cells adopted an elongated, protrusion-rich morphology, with F-actin enriched at the cell periphery and microtubules extending along the protrusion shaft, consistent with a mesenchymal-like invasion program. 3D TFM revealed sustained matrix engagement, including progressive bead clustering, increasing cumulative traction forces, and traction hotspots concentrated near protrusion tips. Perturbation studies separated cytoskeletal requirements for invasion and force transmission: actin polymerization was essential for invasion, myosin II activity was required for robust traction generation and efficient invasion, and microtubule polymerization supported directional persistence and maximal traction output. Notably, a low level of invasion persisted under myosin II inhibition despite minimal detectable traction forces, and this residual invasion was not suppressed by pan-MMP inhibition, indicating a traction-poor, MMP-independent invasion component in Matrigel. Conclusions These findings establish a quantitative mechanical framework for GBM neurosphere invasion in 3D Matrigel and define distinct contributions of actomyosin contractility and microtubules to invasive progression.

title: Quantifying structural variants in chromosomes using landmark-based disparity
abstractText: Abstract Background Chromosomal architecture has played a key role in the evolution of biodiversity. Detecting structural variants (SVs) on chromosomes has informed the study of speciation, sex determination, adaptation, and some of the earliest divergences in the tree of life. Here we present a computationally non-intensive approach based on geometric morphometrics, that uses coordinate data from conserved, single-copy DNA sequences as landmarks to quantify structural disparities of focal chromosomes via primary or haploid genome assemblies across multiple species, individuals, or cell types. Results Based on two approaches, we show that this ‘geno-metric’ method can be applied at micro- and macroevolutionary scales to discover and diagnose SVs. Using human X-linked single-copy genes and ultraconserved elements as genomic ‘landmarks’, we provide empirical demonstrations with amniote sex chromosomes, the Drosophila virilis group, and placental mammal genomes. Landmark-based structural disparity analysis effectively identifies chromosomal SVs and has parallels with traditional morphometrics regarding chromosome size, landmark orientation and landmark availability. Using simulations, we show that structural disparity inferred from ultraconserved elements is correlated with overall levels of chromosome evolution; an attribute which is consistent with observed disparity between and within mammalian orders. We found that the disparity patterns of SVs have significant phylogenetic signal, giving them broad importance for studying evolutionary biology. We also discuss alternative approaches that may be used to extract genomic coordinates and SV data for multi-species comparisons. Conclusions Structural disparity analysis is a reference free, whole-genome alignment free, non-pairwise comparative method that uses coordinates of single-copy genomic markers and dimensionality reduction methods to measure SVs on homologous chromosome sets. The method offers an intuitive, rapid mechanism to detect and measure SVs and consequently, offers the potential to reveal broader patterns of chromosome evolution related to expansions, contractions, rearrangements and phylogenetic history.

title: Enhancing FMCW radar accuracy for adaptive cruise control using CFAR algorithms in adverse weather
abstractText: Abstract Adaptive cruise control (ACC) relies on accurate range and relative-velocity measurements of the preceding vehicle, which frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar provides. Under adverse conditions, however, clutter from rain, fog, and insect swarms degrades these measurements. This study presents a 77 GHz FMCW radar framework for ACC that integrates physically motivated models of rain, fog, and insect clutter with a two-dimensional cell-averaging constant false alarm rate (CA-CFAR) detector. By adapting its threshold to the local clutter level, the detector suppresses clutter-induced peaks and enables more reliable identification of the target response. Simulations up to 200 m show that all three clutter types increase the estimation errors with clutter intensity and distance, and that CFAR processing consistently reduces them. At 83 m under 25 mm/h rain, the range error decreases from 0.50 m to 0.24 m; at 63 m, the velocity error decreases from 4.7% to 2.3%; and at 200 m in dense fog, the range error decreases from 11.25% to 6.20%. The framework detects three targets up to 200 m and resolves velocities as low as 0.0083 m/s, supporting reliable ACC operation in adverse weather.

title: Neural Networks and (Virtual) Extended Formulations
abstractText: Abstract. Neural networks with piecewise linear activation functions, such as rectified linear units (ReLU) or maxout, are among the most fundamental models in modern machine learning. We make a step towards proving lower bounds on the size of such neural networks by linking their representative capabilities to the notion of the extension complexity [Formula: see text] of a polytope [Formula: see text]. This is a well-studied quantity in combinatorial optimization and polyhedral geometry describing the number of inequalities needed to model [Formula: see text] as a linear program. We show that [Formula: see text] is a lower bound on the size of any monotone or input-convex neural network that solves the linear optimization problem over [Formula: see text]. This implies exponential lower bounds on such neural networks for a variety of problems, including the polynomially solvable maximum weight matching problem. In an attempt to prove similar bounds also for general neural networks, we introduce the notion of virtual extension complexity [Formula: see text], which generalizes [Formula: see text] and describes the number of inequalities needed to represent the linear optimization problem over [Formula: see text] as a difference of two linear programs. We prove that [Formula: see text] is a lower bound on the size of any neural network that optimizes over [Formula: see text]. While it remains an open question to derive useful lower bounds on [Formula: see text], we argue that this quantity deserves to be studied independently from neural networks by proving that one can efficiently optimize over a polytope [Formula: see text] given a virtual extended formulation with small encoding size.

title: Latent profiles of moral resilience and associated factors among Chinese nursing interns: a secondary analysis of cross-sectional data
abstractText: Abstract Background: Moral resilience is essential for nursing interns to cope with ethical conflicts during their internships. It is critical to gain insights into the characteristics of moral resilience and understanding its influencing factors to promote professional growth and ethical decision-making skills. Objectives: This study aims to identify the characteristics of moral resilience in nursing interns and explore its influencing factors from demographic, psychological and moral perspectives. Methods: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from four published studies on junior colleges in Hunan Province, China, enrolling 467 nursing interns. Data were collected on demographic characteristics, moral resilience, moral courage, moral sensitivity, and professional identify. Latent profile analysis was employed to categorize moral resilience. Univariate analysis and multinominal logistic regression were used to identify influencing factors. Clinical trial number: not applicable. Results: The data supported a three-profile model of moral resilience: the "low resilience - high efficacy" group (5.14%), the "medium resilience - medium efficacy" group (67.03%), and the "high resilience -low efficacy" group (27.83%). Factors associated with "medium resilience - medium efficacy" group included higher moral courage (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR] = 1.107, P < 0.001). Those with higher moral sensitivity (AOR = 1.053, P = 0.011) and better professional identity (AOR = 0.952, P = 0.026) were more likely to belong to "high resilience -low efficacy" group. Conclusion: This study emphasizes the heterogeneity of moral resilience and its key influencing factors among nursing interns. The findings underscore the importance of tailored psychological interventions to strengthen moral resilience within this group.

abstractText: In this paper we study eigenvalues of Laplacian and biharmonic operators on compact domains in complete manifolds. We establish several new inequalities for eigenvalues of Laplacian and biharmonic operators respectively by using Sobolev type inequalities.

title: Evaluating LLMs on Italian through multi-prompt: the Evalita-LLM benchmark
abstractText: Abstract We present Evalita-LLM, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on Italian tasks. The key innovation of Evalita-LLM is the use of multiple prompts for each task, which mitigates the model’s sensitivity to specific prompt formulations and ensures a robust and objective performance assessment. We propose an iterative methodology for selecting and validating multiple prompts, and metrics that capture both high performance and stability of a prompt given a set of LLMs. The resulting Evalita-LLM multi-prompt benchmark is based on ten native Italian tasks, eliminating translation issues and potential cultural biases. It includes a mix of multiple-choice and generative tasks, enabling more natural interactions with LLMs. We report experimental results from the benchmark’s development phase, along with performance statistics for several state-of-the-art LLMs. Evalita-LLM is publicly available with a leaderboard hosted on Hugging Face to support transparent evaluation and comparison of LLMs.

title: On the Edge Reconstruction of the Second Immanantal Polynomials of Graphs and Digraphs
abstractText: Let $M=(m_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ matrix. The second immanant of matrix $M$ is defined by $d_2(M)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\chi_2(\sigma)\prod_{s=1}^{n}m_{s\sigma(s)}$, where $\chi_2$ is the irreducible character of $S_n$ corresponding to the partition $(2^1,1^{n-2})$. The polynomial $d_2(xI-M)$ is called the second immanantal polynomial of the matrix $M$. Denote by $D(G)$ (resp. $D(\overrightarrow{G})$) and $A(G)$ (resp. $A(\overrightarrow{G})$) the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees (resp. vertex in-degrees) and the adjacency matrix of graph $G$ (resp. digraph $\overrightarrow{G}$), respectively. In this article, we prove that $d_2(xI-A(G))$ (resp. $d_2(xI-A(\overrightarrow{G}))$) can be reconstructed from the second immanantal polynomials of the adjacency matrices of all subgraphs in $\{G-uv,G-u-v\mid uv\in E(G)\}$ (resp. $\{\overrightarrow{G}-e\mid e\in E(\overrightarrow{G})\}$). Furthermore, the polynomial $d_2(xI-D(\overrightarrow{G})\pm A(\overrightarrow{G}))$ can also be reconstructed by the second immanantal polynomials of the Laplacian (signless Laplacian) matrices of all subgraphs in $\{\overrightarrow{G}-e\mid e\in E(\overrightarrow{G})\}$.

title: Predictors of emotional contagion at work in France
abstractText: This research addresses the gap in understanding how various factors influence the spread of emotions in workplace settings, with a specific emphasis on the distinct cultural context of French organizations. Questionnaire data were gathered from a large sample of French permanent employees in France and used vignettes of personal and professional events. Participants were asked to reflect on specific colleagues and rate their emotional responses to various scenarios. Multiple regression analyses assessed the predictors of emotional contagion – such as familiarity, susceptibility, empathy, group climate, communication frequency, and similarity – with emotional contagion measured by respondents’ happiness and sadness in response to the scenarios.Emotional contagion was found to occur twice as much in personal events compared to professional events. Moreover, familiarity emerged as the strongest predictor across all scenarios, highlighting the importance of close interpersonal relationships in emotional contagion. Contrary to expectations, communication frequency and empathy did not consistently predict emotional contagion. The findings underscore the importance of fostering strong interpersonal relationships and supportive organizational environments to enhance emotional well-being and productivity. This could be achieved by French companies through team-building activities and creating supportive work environments.

Experimental study on performance of a two-stroke single cylinder engine applying PODE/methanol/ammonia blends and direct injection strategy
abstractText: In the context of global fuel decarbonization, methanol can substantially reduce soot emissions owing to its high oxygen content. Dissolving ammonia in methanol to form an ammonia–methanol blended fuel can reduce the overall carbon content while enabling ammonia to be incorporated into a liquid fuel mixture. In addition, polyoxymethylene dimethyl ethers, characterized by high oxygen content, high cetane number, and good miscibility with methanol, can compensate for the low reactivity of methanol and ammonia, thereby facilitating fuel preparation and practical application. Therefore, the proposed PODE/methanol/ammonia blending strategy provides a feasible technical pathway for achieving efficient and low-carbon combustion in compression ignition engines. In this study, the performance and emission characteristics of a low-speed two-stroke single-cylinder engine fueled with PODE/methanol blends, PODE/methanol/ammonia blends, and pure PODE were investigated under direct injection mode. The results show that, compared with pure PODE, PODE/methanol and PODE/methanol/ammonia blends shorten combustion duration. For PODE/methanol/ammonia blends, ignition delay is insensitive to injection timing, whereas advancing injection timing effectively shortens combustion duration and increases indicated thermal efficiency by 7.3%. Meanwhile, indicated mean effective pressure and combustion cyclic variation also increase with advanced injection timing. At low load, premixed methanol hinders stable flame propagation, leading to higher cyclic variation. Compared with pure PODE, PODE/methanol/ammonia blends reduce CO 2 emissions by 20.2% and exhibit slightly higher NO X emissions than PODE/methanol blends, but still much lower NO X emissions than pure PODE. Retarding injection timing reduces NO X emissions by 26.1%, but increases CO 2 , CO, and THC emissions. With increasing load, NO X , CO 2 , CO, and THC emissions all decrease. These results demonstrate the combustion feasibility and application potential of PODE/methanol/ammonia blends in diesel engines.

title: Bond Strength of UHPC Overlays on Aging Concrete: Effects of Surface Preparation and Moisture Conditioning
abstractText: Abstract This study investigates the tensile bond performance between ultrahigh-performance concrete (UHPC) overlays and aged normal concrete (NC) substrates under varying surface preparation methods and moisture conditions. A total of 96 laboratory specimens were tested using direct tensile pull-off testing in accordance with ASTM C1583, with 92 specimens retained following outlier screening. Results indicate that substrate moisture condition significantly affects bond performance, with saturated surface conditions increasing system pull-off capacity by approximately 33% relative to dry substrates. Surface preparation methods also played a critical role: abrasive blasting and scarification improved pull-off capacity strength by approximately 30% and 21%, respectively, compared with untreated surfaces. Abrasive blasting combined with saturated surface dry (SSD) conditions produced the highest system bond performance, yielding a 56% improvement over untreated, dry substrates. When macrodamage to coarse aggregate occurred, such as through spalling or scarification, moisture conditioning had minimal influence on bond performance. Exposure to simulated winter conditions and deicing salts further degraded substrate properties, reducing the effectiveness of surface preparation. The findings demonstrate the coupled influence of surface preparation and moisture conditioning on UHPC–NC bond performance and provide practical guidance for mitigating delamination risks in UHPC overlay applications for aging infrastructure.

title: Future projections of distribution dynamics and biomass of dwarf bamboos in northern Japan using a dynamic global vegetation model
abstractText: Abstract Dwarf bamboo (DB) species are widespread across East Asia, including northern Japan, where they form pure communities and strongly influence ecosystem structure and vegetation dynamics, including tree regeneration. The regional distribution of different DB types is strongly associated with maximum snow depth, which is expected to decrease under future warming. Climate-induced changes in snow conditions may therefore alter both the distribution and biomass of DB vegetation. However, dwarf bamboo and its sensitivity to snow conditions have rarely been represented in vegetation models, such as dynamic global vegetation models, which limits our ability to project the effect and change of DB under climate change. In this study, we developed a dwarf bamboo submodule within the SEIB-DGVM framework to simulate future changes in the distribution and aboveground biomass (AGB) of DB species in Hokkaido, northern Japan. Under the RCP8.5 scenario, our simulations indicate that Sasa nipponica , a smaller species adapted to shallower snow conditions, is likely to expand its distribution. Across three different climate datasets under the RCP8.5 scenario, an average of 72.8% of the grid cells classified as the tall-stature type under the present-day climate were projected to shift to the short-stature type. Simulated AGB responses differed depending on whether the dominant DB type remained stable or shifted between types. Across all grid cells, mean AGB decreased by 403 g DM m⁻ 2 , corresponding to approximately 16.1% decrease relative to the current climate. Our results demonstrate that climate-driven reductions in snow depth can cause substantial shifts in the distribution and biomass of dwarf bamboo. Explicitly representing these snow-mediated vegetation shifts in DGVMs may therefore improve projections of non-tree vegetation dynamics under climate change. The developed model provides a framework for evaluating future changes in dwarf bamboo vegetation and their ecological consequences in northern Japan.

title: Dynamic electrical control of on-chip second-harmonic generation with ferroelectric NbOBr2
abstractText: Abstract Niobium oxide dihalides such as NbOCl2, featured by vanishing interlayer electronic coupling, present thickness-scalable strong second-harmonic generation (SHG), which has demonstrated their compelling performance of free-space nonlinear optics (NLO). However, practical on-chip photonic applications demand not only high NLO efficiency but also robust electrical tunability, a critical capability that has remained elusive until now. Our work reports the first realization of an in-situ electrically tunable NLO response within a NbOBr2-photonic integrated circuit (PIC). This material uniquely combines two critical features: exceptional tunability enabled by in-plane ferroelectricity and a strong second-order susceptibility resulting from its intrinsic broken-inversion symmetry. In this on-chip photonic circuitry scenario, NbOBr2 showcases larger SHG efficiency than NbOCl2 because of its low index contrast and completely outperforms NbOCl2 in the modulation capability thanks to much stronger in-plane ferroelectricity of NbOBr2. We achieve dynamic, non-volatile SHG intensity modulation exceeding 53%, with polarization states retained even after removing the external electric field. This work establishes the integration of 2D ferroelectric NbOBr2 into PICs as a transformative approach for developing scalable and reconfigurable ultracompact NLO devices, opening new avenues for versatile applications in tunable light sources, optical information processing, and quantum photonics.

title: More than Just Measurement Models? Processing Insights from Population Coding Models of Visual Working Memory Retrieval
abstractText: Abstract Continuous memory retrieval tasks provide a precise measure of visual working memory (VWM), but the mechanisms underlying their heavy-tailed error distributions remain debated. Recent population coding models (PCMs), including the neural resource model , target confusability competition model , and signal discrimination model , explain such errors as the outcome of noisy signals distributed over feature space. These models share a common tuning–noise–decoding structure but differ in their tuning functions, noise distributions, decoding rules, and process-level interpretations. Across two colour reproduction experiments, we tested how memory load and stimulus identifiability are expressed within this shared framework. In Experiment 1, participants remembered colour arrays varying in set size and stimulus saturation. In Experiment 2, we factorially manipulated stimulus and response-wheel saturation while varying set size. We first compared models formed by crossing von Mises and Laplace-like tuning functions with Normal, Gumbel, and Poisson noise distributions. We then tested whether set-size effects and saturation effects were selectively identified in the amplitude parameter $$\:\gamma\:$$ and dispersion parameter $$\:\kappa\:$$ , respectively. Finally, we evaluated whether the set-size effect followed a sample-size model constraint, or its more flexible power-law generalisation. We found that the preferred tuning function varied across individuals, whereas Normal and Gumbel noise generally provided better fits than Poisson noise. Model comparisons supported separable effects of memory load and stimulus identifiability, captured selectively by changes in $$\:\gamma\:$$ and $$\:\kappa\:$$ . Across both experiments, $$\:\gamma\:$$ decreased closely following a square-root law with set size, supporting the prediction of sample-size model. Our findings provide direct empirical evidence supporting that PCMs do more than measure continuous error distributions: their parameters provide identifiable links between empirical VWM performances and fundamental cognitive constructs, including memory capacity limits and the structure of mental stimulus representations.

title: Single‐Cell Identification of Bacterivorous Mixotrophs in a Freshwater Habitat
abstractText: ABSTRACT The nutritional strategy of phago‐mixotrophy among pigmented eukaryotes has been widely recognized and characterized across various taxonomic lineages. While their ecological role as bacterivores in different aquatic environments is acknowledged, establishing a clear connection between phago‐mixotrophic activities and taxonomy within natural communities remains challenging. In this study, we utilized a combination of microscopy and fluorescence‐activated single‐cell sorting techniques to investigate the diversity and temporal variations of bacteria‐feeding mixotrophs in a freshwater habitat. We identified four groups of mixotrophs using both methods: Pedinellales (Dictyochophyceae), Cryptomonas (Cryptophyceae), Dinobryon (Chrysophyceae) and a single‐chloroplast bearing group within Chlorophyta. Together, these groups accounted for 58%–96% and 54%–95% of total mixotrophs detected by microscopy and cell sorting, respectively. Samples collected in different seasons demonstrated that Pedinellales and Chlorophyta were more abundant in spring and summer/autumn, while Dinobryon was only present in winter when temperatures were lowest and light intensity was moderate. Our findings, with 6 classes and 12 genera identified as bacterivorous mixotrophs, highlight the promising potential of single‐cell techniques in aquatic microbiology. This approach reveals the taxonomic identity and feeding activities of phago‐mixotrophs in situ, thereby enhancing our understanding of their functional ecological roles within microbial food webs.

title: Endothelial KLK8 Promotes Diabetic Nephropathy via a LIFR Dependent Mechanism
abstractText: Abstract Background Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is the primary microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus; however, the exact pathways in endothelial cells (ECs) linked to DN progress remain unclear. Tissue kallikrein-related peptidases (KLKs) participate in pathophysiological processes in ECs. We aimed to explore the roles of endothelial KLKs in DN and define the underlying mechanisms. Methods and results KLK8 was the most highly upregulated member of KLKs in renal tissues in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic mice and cultured glomerular ECs (GECs) upon high glucose (HG) treatment. Both global (Klk8 -/- ) and endothelial Klk8 knockout (Klk8 ΔEC ) mice displayed improved albuminuria, mesangial matrix expansion and glomerulosclerosis caused by STZ compared to Klk8 f/f mice. Single-cell RNA seq (scRNA-seq) showed that many pathways associated with DN in ECs, mesangial cells (MCs) and tubule cells were reversed in Klk8 ΔEC mice. Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) was extensively improved in Klk8 ΔEC mice, and by KLK8 siRNA in cultured GECs upon HG. Using proteome and other biochemical approaches, we revealed that KLK8 cleaved syndecan-4(SDC4), which contributed to loss of glycocalyx integrity in GECs in cultured cells and animal diabetic models. Furthermore, scRNA-seq showed that Lifr was one of the key genes linked to the disease progressed in ECs and MCs and regulated by endothelial Klk8. LIFR signaling contributed to HG-induced GEC dysfunction and MC activation, which was associated with endothelial Klk8. Knockdown of Lifr by lentivirus-Lifr shRNA ameliorated hallmark features of DN and improved EndMT and Sdc4 expression glomeruli of diabetic mice. LIFR was upregulated in GECs and MCs in DN patients. Circulatory levels of LIF, KLK8 and soluble SDC4 were increased in patients with DN, and KLK8 level was positively correlated with LIF, soluble SDC4 and creatinine levels. Conclusion Endothelial KLK8 promotes GECs dysfunction and abnormal crosstalk with MCs through a LIFR-dependent signaling in DN, which immediately highlights therapeutic targets for DN.
